边界与约束采样\\\\n\\\\n结构化生成不是把一个固定模板贴在输出上，而是把语言模型的条件分布限制在目标语言从当前前缀仍可完成的延伸上。每次采样既改变已生成文本，也改变语法解析状态；token 可以跨多个语法边界，因而首字符检查不可能代替完整展开。\\\\n\\\\n## 问题定义：字符语言、token 展开与请求状态\\\\n\\\\n设目标语言 L⊆Σ*，上下文无关语法 G=(N,Σ,P,S)。词表 V 中每个 token v 对应有限串 σ(v)∈Σ*；EOS 是特殊终止 token，不属于普通文本展开。字节级实现可令 Σ={0,...,255}，因而一个 token 可包含不完整的 UTF-8 字节。字符级实现只是 Σ 的另一种选择。\\\\n\\\\n用下推自动机表示 CFG。一个变体是 P=(R,Σ,{A_r}_{r∈R},q_main,δ)，其中 A_r=(Q_r,Σ∪R,q^start_r,F_r,δ_r) 表示规则 r 的有限状态自动机；字符边消耗输入，规则引用边压栈并进入子规则，子规则接受后弹栈回到父规则。解析状态通常不是单个栈，而是一组配置 S={(stack_i,q_i)}，因为语法可能非确定，同一个输入字符可分叉到多条规则展开。stack 记录返回规则和返回节点，q_i 是当前节点；输入全部读完、栈为空且到达接受节点才算接受。\\\\n\\\\n对请求保存已确认 token 序列 y、解析状态 S、生成代次 g 和缓存身份 κ。若普通生成从答案起点开始，S 从 q_main 初始化；若 chat template 通过 continue_final_message 等方式预填了部分 assistant 内容，例如已给出 JSON 前缀，S 必须从该受约束前缀的解析结果开始，而不是从根重新开始。否则会把已经存在的字符重新约束一遍，或把前缀中的引号、括号当成新输出。\\\\n\\\\n给定 S，合法 token 集定义为 A(S)={v∈V : advance(S,σ(v)) 至少含一个仍可到达接受状态的配置}，并在 S 可接受时加入 EOS。这里的关键词是仍可到达接受状态：一个暂未闭合字符串的 token 可以合法，只要后面存在完成路径；相反，一个首字符看似正确但使剩余栈无法完成的 token 不合法。\\\\n\\\\n若原模型在给定上下文下的分布为 p，约束采样的一种基本语义是 p'(x)=p(x)/Z_S（x∈A(S)），否则 p'(x)=0，其中 Z_S=Σ_{x∈A(S)}p(x)。若 Z_S=0，说明没有合法概率质量，应报告失败或执行声明的恢复路径，不能静默解除约束。温度、惩罚、top-k、top-p 和投机验证会改变 p；最终实现必须明确这些变换与 grammar mask 的顺序，并保证最终支持集包含于 A(S)。\\\\n\\\\n## 合法性：语法状态、输入语义与采样边界\\\\n\\\\n目标语言、tokenizer 和请求起点的身份都属于合法性条件。词表 V 不是抽象的整数集合：token id 通过 tokenizer 版本映射到字节串 σ(v)。tokenizer 合并规则、特殊 token 表或词表版本改变后，同一个 id 可能对应不同文本，旧 mask 缓存不能继续使用。chat template 也可能插入角色控制 token、BOS/EOS 或 generation prompt；这些 token 定义模型实际消费的输入，但它们通常不属于受 JSON/XML 语法约束的 assistant 输出区间。实现必须显式记录受约束区间的起点。\\\\n\\\\nJSON 语法合法与 JSON Schema 的全部语义约束不是同一层。CFG 适合表达括号、引号、转义、嵌套和递归结构；字段是否存在、类型、数值范围、跨字段依赖和业务含义，需要 schema 校验、专用自动机或后处理。把某条 schema 约束编译进语法是可能的工程选择，但语法解析成功不能自动证明这些语义成立。\\\\n\\\\nEOS 只有在当前状态接受时才合法。达到最大 token 数而语法尚未接受，是未完成或失败，不是格式正确；finish reason 应保留这个区别。空合法集合同样不能被当成模型没有偏好而回退到无约束采样。若实现因数值下溢导致合法质量全为零，也应显式报告，而不是抽取被屏蔽 token。\\\\n\\\\n在批量执行中，mask、grammar 状态和随机状态按请求与逻辑分支索引，不能按当前 batch 槽位索引。槽位压紧、请求完成、取消或投机分支重排后，身份映射必须仍然正确。对含多个解析配置的状态，合法 token 是各配置可接受 token 的并集；不能用某一个栈的 mask 代替整个状态。\\\\n\\\\n## 从 PDA 到可用 mask 的算法\\\\n\\\\n直接在每个 decode 步对全词表逐字符执行 PDA 代价很高。可把每个自动机节点 q 的 token 分成三类：与完整栈无关的接受集 I_q^+、拒绝集 I_q^-，以及需要回看父规则的依赖集 D_q。以节点为键预计算前两类；运行时只对 D_q 逐 token 展开，最后把结果与各并行配置的 mask 合并。语法展开、规则内联和 expanded suffix 预计算都是为了缩小 D_q。\\\\n\\\\nXGrammar 的机制进一步给出上下文扩展：对每条规则预计算从父规则返回后可能接受的字符串集合；依赖 token 的剩余部分若不是该集合的前缀或起始串，就可以在预处理阶段判为拒绝。论文在 Llama-3.1、128k 词表和 JSON 语法下报告依赖上下文 token 从 1134 降到 120，cache 从 160 MB 降到 0.46 MB。这些是论文报告的数字，不是本库在目标硬件上的测量。\\\\n\\\\n一个可实现的单请求步骤如下：\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 按语法状态生成一个请求的 token\\\\n输入：请求 r，已确认受约束输出 y，语法 G，tokenizer 映射 σ，最大步数 M\\\\n输出：追加 token，或声明完成/失败\\\\nκ ← (G.version, tokenizer.version, vocab.version, byte_mode, cache_format)\\\\n(P, cache) ← 取得或编译 κ 对应的 PDA 与预计算 cache\\\\nS ← q_main 的初始配置集合\\\\n若 y 是已有的受约束前缀（例如 continue_final_message 的 JSON 前缀）：\\\\n    S ← advance(S, bytes(y))\\\\n    若 S 为空：报告初始化失败\\\\nfor step = 1..M:\\\\n    若 S 为空：报告状态错误，不能继续采样\\\\n    C ← 从 cache 取各栈顶节点的预计算合法 token 并集\\\\n    for v in D(S):                         // 需要完整栈检查的候选\\\\n        if advance(S, σ(v)) 仍有可接受延伸:\\\\n            C ← C ∪ {v}\\\\n    if S 可接受:\\\\n        C ← C ∪ {EOS}\\\\n    if C 为空:\\\\n        返回失败，不解除约束\\\\n    logits'[v] ← logits[v] if v ∈ C else -∞\\\\n    p' ← 按声明顺序应用温度、惩罚、截断与 softmax\\\\n    保证 support(p') ⊆ C\\\\n    v ← sample(p', 请求 r 的随机流)\\\\n    S' ← advance(S, σ(v))\\\\n    if S' 为空:\\\\n        报告实现或 cache 身份错误\\\\n    S ← S'\\\\n    提交 v 到已确认输出\\\\n    if v = EOS:\\\\n        返回完成\\\\n返回未完成\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n这里没有把 mask 生成写成先拿上一 token 的 mask 套在新 logits 上。mask 由已确认 token 之后的状态决定；如果 mask 异步生成，必须携带状态代次，迟到的旧 mask 不能用于新 logits。采样与 grammar mask 的顺序也必须在实现中固定，否则 top-p 阈值到底作用于原分布还是限制后的分布会产生不同结果。\\\\n\\\\n预计算 cache 还要选择存储格式。对每个节点，若独立接受集很大，可存拒绝 token 列表和依赖 token 列表；若拒绝集很大，可存接受 token 列表和依赖 token 列表；当两侧接近时使用词表大小的 bitset。多个并行栈合并时，不能简单把一个栈的接受集当成最终答案，而应对所有可达配置求并集，或在接受/拒绝表示下做等价的集合运算。\\\\n\\\\n分支和回滚需要解析状态所有权。persistent stack 把多个时刻和多个候选的栈组织成一棵树，每个分支保存栈顶指针；分叉只增加路径，不复制整条栈。接受一条投机路径时，KV、随机状态、输出缓冲和 grammar 状态应在同一确认边界提交；拒绝时回退到最后一个接受位置，兄弟分支不能共享可变的父规则返回栈。\\\\n\\\\nCPU 生成 mask 与 GPU 前向可以重叠的条件是：mask 只依赖已经确认的前缀 token，而当前前向也只依赖同一前缀；在采样前同步。预编译和 prefill 也可以部分重叠。若 mask 依赖尚未提交的候选 token，或 batch 中 CPU 已饱和，这种重叠就不能按理想关键路径相加。\\\\n\\\\n## 一个可手算的小语言\\\\n\\\\n为了区分首字符检查和完整展开，取有限语法 S → '[' E ']'、E → ε | V | V ',' V、V → 'a' | 'b' | '[' F ']'、F → ε | W | W ',' W、W → 'a' | 'b'。它接受 []、[a]、[b]、[a,b]、[[a]]、[[a,b]] 等串，最大嵌套只用于说明栈状态，不声称覆盖完整 JSON。\\\\n\\\\n在空前缀后，token a,b] 展开为 [a,b]，合法；token a,] 展开为 [a,]，不合法。前缀 [a 后，token ]] 得到 [a]]，不合法；前缀 [[a 后，同样的 ]] 得到 [[a]]，合法。前缀 [] 已经接受，EOS 合法；若把 EOS 排除，任何普通 token 都会走向多余字符。这个例子说明：合法性与当前栈的深度、当前规则节点和 token 的完整展开同时有关。\\\\n\\\\n把该有限语言的所有接受串枚举出来，可以作为独立参考：对任意前缀 y 和 token v，只要存在某个接受串以 yσ(v) 开头，v 就合法。这个参考不调用 PDA 实现，适合检查首字符启发式、漏掉 token 尾部或错误处理 EOS 的实现。下面的检查文件就是这一思路的 CPU 逻辑验证。\\\\n\\\\n## 成本：编译、每 token、传输、驻留与同步\\\\n\\\\n设词表大小为 |V|，依赖上下文候选数为 D，token 平均字节数为 L̄，并行栈数为 b。朴素做法每个请求步扫描全词表并逐字符执行 PDA，成本量级为 |V|·L̄ 的字符转移；预计算后，每步主要付出 cache 查表、D 个依赖候选的展开、b 个配置的 mask 合并和同步成本。可写成 T_mask ≈ c_lookup + D·L̄·c_char + b·c_merge + c_sync；这些项是否在关键路径上取决于实现，不能直接与 GPU 前向时间相加。\\\\n\\\\n预编译成本发生在 grammar、tokenizer 或 cache 格式首次出现时，包括 PDA 构造、内联、上下文扩展和逐节点预计算。复杂语法可能提高首次请求延迟，却降低后续每 token 的在线检查量。把编译隐藏在预热中只能说明稳定服务的一个阶段，不能证明冷启动具有同样延迟。\\\\n\\\\n通信成本要看 mask 的表示。若向设备传完整 bitset，每个请求每步约 ceil(|V|/8) 字节；128k 词表时约 16 KiB，batch 为 B 时约 B 倍，另加固定传输与同步延迟。若只传接受 token 列表，大小随合法集变化，可能更小，也可能在宽接受集下更大。若采样核在设备上直接读 mask，则省去这次回传，但 mask 仍要在 CPU 或其他设备上生成。容量、带宽和同步延迟必须按同一 batch 与同一时间窗口列账。\\\\n\\\\n驻留成本包括预编译 PDA、每节点 cache、请求解析栈、分支快照和临时 mask 缓冲。persistent stack 让相邻状态共享深层栈节点，分叉和回滚通常只需改指针；这不消除 token 匹配本身的字符处理，也不自动让跨设备状态零成本。取消请求时要释放解析状态和设备 mask 缓冲，但在途执行仍可能持有引用，回收要等最后使用者完成。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化后的保留、调整与放弃\\\\n\\\\nbatch 增大时，GPU 前向可能更饱满，但 CPU mask 生成、集合合并和同步压力也增大。若 mask 时间仍小于前向，重叠可以保留；若 CPU 成为瓶颈，应改为批量化、并行化或把部分工作移到设备，而不是假设批越大越能隐藏。语法越复杂、嵌套越深，依赖上下文 token 越多，预处理和 cache 内存越重要；对简单正则或极短输出，复杂 CFG 引擎可能只增加编译和状态管理成本。\\\\n\\\\ntokenizer、词表、模板或 grammar 版本变化应使相关 cache 退出可用集合。若请求通过 chat template 预填了部分 assistant 输出，改变模板或 generation prompt 也会改变受约束区间的起点，不能沿用按旧起点生成的 mask。对前缀缓存和恢复，已确认输出可以重放以重建解析状态，但必须使用同一 grammar/tokenizer 版本；不同版本下看起来相同的 token 前缀不保证同一字节串。\\\\n\\\\n叠加投机解码时，草稿分支需要自己的 grammar 状态。目标验证的接受/修正比必须使用实际约束后的 p' 和 q'；某个草稿分支合法，只说明它有正概率，不代表它按目标分布被选择。树形候选的兄弟路径不能共享可变解析栈；拒绝后 grammar、KV、随机状态和输出要一起回退。若接受率下降或 grammar 使候选支持集过窄，应减少或关闭投机，而不是绕过约束。\\\\n\\\\n取消与故障恢复要把 grammar 状态和 mask 代次纳入请求状态，见[推理服务恢复](../system-semantics/serving-recovery.md)。恢复时可从已确认 token 重放解析，但迟到 mask、旧分支状态和已失效缓存不能重新获得提交权。\\\\n\\\\n## 诊断：竞争解释与区分实验\\\\n\\\\n输出不合法可能有多种解释：mask 生成错、tokenizer 映射错、chat template 起点错、EOS 或最大长度处理错、schema 语义未校验，或者模型只是质量差但格式正确。区分实验要针对每种解释给出不同预测。\\\\n\\\\n第一类是有限语言穷举：用小词表和短语法枚举所有接受串，对每个前缀和 token 比较运行时 mask 与独立参考。它能直接发现只看首字符的假阳性，也能发现漏掉 token 尾部、错误弹栈和 EOS 错误。负对照应故意使用首字符启发式，并确认检查确实拒绝它；如果检查对错误实现也给通过，说明 oracle 没有辨别力。\\\\n\\\\n第二类是空合法集和终止边界。已有接受前缀只应允许 EOS；若实现返回空 mask 却继续无约束采样，会立即出现非法 token。未接受状态达到长度上限应保留未完成原因，不能标记为格式成功。\\\\n\\\\n第三类是 cache 身份。改变 tokenizer 对某个 token 的字节映射或 grammar 版本，旧 cache 应失效；若输出只在切换版本后出现非法字符，优先检查 cache 键而不是模型。第四类是异步代次。注入一个迟到 mask，确认新 token 不消费旧代次结果；若错误只在取消或重排后出现，检查状态所有权和完成通知。\\\\n\\\\n第五类是 schema 语义。构造语法合法但类型、范围或跨字段关系错误的 JSON，语法检查应通过而 schema 校验应失败；两类检查不能互相代替。性能诊断则分别记录编译、每 token mask、传输、前向和采样时间，再比较重叠前后关键路径。没有这些分项，不能用端到端总时间反推某个优化有效。\\\\n\\\\n上述有限语言检查是 CPU 逻辑验证；它不证明目标 GPU 上的 mask 传输、CPU/GPU 重叠或服务吞吐。论文报告和本库公式也只支持各自条件下的机制与成本预测。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 正文与算法\\\\n\\\\n正文以问题和机制展开：说明问题为什么出现，定义对象和合法性，展开算法、数据流与状态更新，推导成本与组合关系，用设定算例、反例和区分实验解释结论如何改变。篇幅与结构由内容决定，不规定候选数、反例数或统一段落数量。\\\\n\\\\n实现逻辑可以转写为完整的算法伪代码，使用 pseudocode 联网补全。准确版本留作证据身份；只有影响本题合法性或成本的版本事实进入论证，不搬运与本题无关的参数和分支。\\\\n\\\\n## 逐层阅读\\\\n\\\\n阅读入口按主题地图、章节摘要与问题/前提、二级节结构、完整论证、来源原文展开。Agent 自主选择阅读深度；索引与检索结果提供相邻机制，不产生必读清单。读取按实际字符范围与冻结修订记录；读过摘要不等于读过整章。\\\\n\\\\n## Base、观测和 workflow\\\\n\\\\nBase 的来源事实受发布版本的时间上限约束；编辑日期不改变事实日期。新的整理和独立推导保留真实日期与依据，后续实验不能伪装成历史 seed。\\\\n\\\\n运行观测保存环境、workload、测量方法、数值/单位/不确定性、实验证据与真实日期。机制知识解释因果、条件、预测和反例。Workflow 保存一类局部设计、诊断或验证问题的触发条件、前提、步骤、检查与退出/调整条件、成本和复用边界。三者相互引用，不能用一次成功代替机制解释或跨条件验证。\\\\n\\\\nEvolution 提炼、Diagnostician 独立复核，沿已有发布和证据机制进入后续冻结、检索与读取。Workflow 为可选方法，不自动成为 Controller 的全局顺序。跨任务资格使用现有权威晋升机制，负面与不确定结果保留，不建立平行资格体系。\\\\n\\\\n## 修订、覆盖和验证\\\\n\\\\n已有技术对象优先深化原章；独立对象才新增章节。修订保存登记前正文与元数据的准确字节，更新 catalog、来源说明哈希、导航、时间审计、VERSION 与变更清单。已存在的来源归档保持原身份。\\\\n\\\\n覆盖审计同时检查能力域、具体算法与跨机制组合，区分完整解释、仅提及、缺少推导、缺少证据和缺失；篇数和术语命中不是覆盖证明。结构/身份检查、独立算法算例、运行时读取/发布测试与真实构建效果分别报告。通过前几项不能声称已证明知识改善了 Agent 的系统设计或性能。\\\\n\\\\n六项标准的具体追问、组合案例、来源核对和使用效果边界见[知识内容审查](knowledge-review.md)。[Attention \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"required\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# 知识内容审查：从 Attention 样例推广\\\\n\\\\n本页把 Attention 多轮审查发现的问题整理为内容作者与审阅者可复用的问题。依据是[知识库构建方法](knowledge-method.md)中的六项标准，深度样例是[当前 Attention 模块](attention-module.md)。它不增加 Agent 的角色义务，也不要求每章采用同一结构、同样多的算例或统一的工程路线。\\\\n\\\\n## 知识库承担什么任务\\\\n\\\\n本库支持 InfraAgents 根据模型、workload、硬件和服务目标，从空工程构建、检验与持续优化完整推理系统。知识应提供五种帮助：还原问题的理论基础；区分合法条件与可探索的设计空间；给出足以独立实现的算法与状态关系；支持成本预测、实验和诊断；保存能够被反驳、修正和迁移的经验。\\\\n\\\\n一条有用的阅读链应支持读者形成这样的推理：任务与输入条件 → 正确性要求 → 候选算法与数据流 → 成本预测 → 区分实验 → 实现结果 → 修正后的结论。某一章可以承担其中一部分，但承担核心算法的地方不能只列注意事项或把关键步骤交给源码。\\\\n\\\\n## 六项标准怎样落实到实际问题\\\\n\\\\n| 内容标准 | 审阅时实际追问 | 过去发现的问题及其含义 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 原因、数学定义、输入输出和状态 | 为什么需要这个机制？每个量的轴、单位、范围和身份是什么？状态代表已知、已算、已确认还是已分配？ | FP8 只写“使用块尺度”不足以恢复分数和 PV 的共同单位；调度中的 token 已生成不等于其 KV 已计算 |\\\\n| 合法性与方案选择 | 哪条性质来自函数、数值契约或设备语义，哪条来自某个方案？等价性在实数、浮点还是特定误差范围内成立？ | 精确算术的归约结合性不能直接变成浮点逐位相同；图地址稳定不证明数据身份仍正确；内部 fragment 未公开就不能猜 lane 映射 |\\\\n| 算法、数据流和状态变化 | 能否写出初始化、推进、提交和结束？第一块、最后一块、空输入和失败分支怎样处理？每个被消费的量从哪里产生？ | 量化流程需要量化与恢复尺度；缓冲需要生产者、所有消费者及代次；硬件专题需要一条从逻辑 tile 到地址、线程、片上布局、指令输入和写回的完整路径 |\\\\n| 六类成本 | 是否在同一候选、相同输入和相同时间范围中列账？哪些量可以相加，哪些受关键路径和共享资源限制？ | 唯一 KV、各 head 请求流量和 DRAM 事务不能混算；共享容量只计一次；预留池与其中存活对象不能重复相加；深流水的驻留和 spill 会改变本来用于估时的吞吐 |\\\\n| 条件变化后的选择 | 改变 shape、状态组织、精度、到达轨迹或设备能力，哪条依赖保留，哪项成本改变？何种结果足以推翻原选择？ | 更多分区在并行度不足时有利，在已经饱和时可能只增加合并；更多缓冲不保证更快；缓存命中不保证新请求可立即执行 |\\\\n| 区分竞争解释 | 观察支持哪些解释？它们对某个可控改变给出什么不同预测？实验结果不符后怎样修改判断？ | “三级比两级慢”同时允许首尾、spill、驻留和未重叠解释；一次时间测量不能决定原因；软件事件模型不能证明 GPU 的内存可见性 |\\\\n\\\\n这些问题由主题决定使用范围。调度章节需要把就绪性、预算和输出归属连起来；缓存章节需要贯通身份、复制、发布和回收；硬件章节需要贯通布局、执行契约和资源。协议、统计或模型语义章节不必凭空增加矩阵指令实例。\\\\n\\\\n## 从单个机制走到组合案例\\\\n\\\\n分开解释各个机制之后，选择会改变合法性或成本的真实交界，追踪一次完整变化。例如共享前缀和私有尾块在追加、封存、发布、消费与回收期间，内容、scale、页表和读者必须属于一致的状态；调度器选中的工作必须已有上游输入和容量，而执行视图的压紧不能改变请求归属。\\\\n\\\\n审阅者沿一次轨迹检查：发生了什么输入事件；哪些对象仍存活；谁能写；谁已经取得读取权；何时对消费者可见；失败后哪些旧状态仍有效；取消后哪些工作仍在途；何时能把同一物理资源交给下一使用者。对象需要身份或代次时，解释防止的具体错误。只有单次同步执行的算法不必引入多代次协议。\\\\n\\\\n交界还包括“看似已经完成，下一步却没有输入”的状态。本轮调度审阅发现：完整命中 KV 而没有末行 logits 时，只按已知长度减 KV 长度选择工作会得到零，无法生成第一个新 token。修订明确了安全重算最后一个已知 token 的路径及共享写区隔离。沿状态图检查是否存在有合法请求却无后继事件的停滞，比只检查各状态的字段范围更有用。\\\\n\\\\n组合案例应使读者能计算至少一项会影响决定的代价，并解释另一种选择何时反转。重点是让独立机制能够正确拼接，不是枚举所有组合。示例的页长、tile、队列策略和版本字段均为可替换选择。\\\\n\\\\n## 阅读链与事实核对\\\\n\\\\n先检查正文承担的核心知识，再检查直接来源说明与足以支持关键事实的固定论文或文档。保留原始资料的错误、版本身份和字节，在解释中纠正公式或限定结论；自己的推导不能归为论文实测。源码可以用于作者核对，但读者独立实现所需的事实应进入允许读取的算法说明。\\\\n\\\\n审查记录写明读过哪些正文、哪些来源及其范围、发现的具体问题、实际修改与检查。只有读取摘要、术语检索或运行链接检查的专题，继续保留深度复核待完成状态。没有必要为了一个确定问题递归阅读所有引用。\\\\n\\\\n## 内容与使用效果分别验收\\\\n\\\\n内容审查判断六项标准在声明范围内是否有充分解释。作者侧算例验证代数、布局、边界、协议或成本模型；它需要独立参考、不变量或能触发错误的负对照，不能只让测试复述实现。读取测试检查冻结内容能否被取回及身份是否匹配。这三类证据各自有效，不能互相代替。\\\\n\\\\n直接使用检验让 Agent 在没有现成实现的情况下处理正文未直接演示的问题：重新推导合法算法，改变输入或硬件条件后重算，面对错误提出竞争解释，收到反证后修改方案。保存允许资料、任务、模型/上下文、预算、答卷或实现、执行结果及失败归因。交叉审阅兼做推导练习可以发现内容缺口，但有共同上下文、作者经验或未隔离的环境时，只能声称完成这次练习。\\\\n\\\\n如果要声称“知识改善了 Agent 的构建能力”，还需可比的知识版本或对照条件、多个代表任务以及预先说明的判断方法。目标 GPU 的数值、同步、重叠和性能仍需设备结果。没有最佳 tile 或流水级数不构成知识缺陷；没有解释如何推导候选、识别限制、测量与修正，才是内容缺口。\\\\n\\\\n## 怎样给出审查结论\\\\n\\\\n对每个问题给出正文位置、明确结论与证据边界，区分“已完整解释”“仅提及”“缺推导”“缺证据”“缺失”。这些描述可按实际内容组合使用，不转成总分或用测试数量抵消关键算法缺口。\\\\n\\\\n已经修复的问题在新修订中复核后关闭，不沿用旧审查中“仍缺 FP8/硬件映射/组合案例”的判断。新的缺口必须来自当前字节。Attention 当前的两个具体案例已补足内容展开，实际 Agent 独立构建与目标 GPU 效果仍有各自的验证边界。以当前内容和当前证据决定结论，不为了持续审查而不断增加验收条件。\\\\n\\\\n扩展工作优先完成相关专题的一条知识链，再复核跨专题衔接。当前批次与逐篇状态见[扩展状态](expansion-status.json)；历史审查保留当时结论，不覆盖成当前状态。\\\\n\\\", 边界与约束采样\\\\n\\\\n结构化生成将语法状态与语言模型状态同步推进，合法 token 是从当前语法状态仍可完成目标语言的延伸。\\\\n\\\\n## 字符语言与 token 语言之间\\\\n\\\\nJSON、正则和上下文无关语法通常描述字符或字节串，模型却按 token 生成。一个 token 可能跨越多个语法边界，也可能只是一段 UTF-8 字节。合法性判断要将 token 的展开内容作用到当前解析状态，而不能只检查其首字符。接受一个暂未完成字符串的 token 可以合法，只要后面仍存在可接受的完成路径。\\\\n\\\\n语法状态可包括栈、字符串转义状态、未完成字节和已生成的结构字段。EOS 只有在当前状态允许结束时才合法。JSON 格式合法与 JSON Schema 的全部语义约束不是同一层：字段类型、范围、跨字段关系和业务含义需要各自对应的表达能力或后续验证。\\\\n\\\\n## 约束怎样进入分布\\\\n\\\\n设当前合法 token 集 A(s)，新分布 p′(x) 在 x∈A(s) 时与 p(x) 成比例，其余为零。这样改变了原模型分布，但满足规定语言。采样完成后，语法状态沿实际选中的 token 前进。将 grammar mask 提前计算并与 GPU 前向重叠，要求所用状态已确认；不能拿上一 token 之前的 mask 套在新 logits 上。\\\\n\\\\n大量 token 的合法性与具体栈上下文无关，可预计算；剩余 token 才需要在线解析。XGrammar 的设计利用了这种分离。词表、tokenizer 和语法版本共同决定预计算结果，模型换 tokenizer 后沿用旧 mask 缓存不成立。\\\\n\\\\n## 与投机、取消和多租户的组合\\\\n\\\\n投机分支需要对应的语法分支状态；拒绝候选后回到最后接受位置。共享不可变的编译语法可以节省成本，但每请求的解析栈、已消费位置和输出不能共用可变对象。取消需要释放解析状态和设备 mask 缓冲区，同时保留在途执行的生命周期。\\\\n\\\\n结构化输出性能取决于模型前向、mask 生成和传输的关键路径。预编译较复杂语法可能增加首次请求延迟，却提高后续吞吐。若把编译隐藏在预热里，应将冷启动与稳定服务分别建模。Agent 应从语言表达能力、逐 token 状态同步和缓存身份推导接入方式，再选择库提供的接口。\\\\n\\\\n## 约束状态也是分支状态\\\\n\\\\n一个树形候选需要自己的解析状态快照或可重放路径；兄弟分支不能共享可变解析栈。接受一条路径时，与 KV、随机状态和输出一起提交到同一位置，拒绝后撤销未确认的 mask/解析推进。预先生成 mask 的异步工作要携带状态代次，迟到 mask 不得用于新 token 的 logits。\\\\n\\\\n应用 constraint mask 后的目标分布，与无约束原分布不同。若叠加投机，p/q 修正必须对应实际约束与截断顺序；某个草稿分支合法不等于它按目标概率被选择。grammar 编译缓存可以共享不可变内容，但 tokenizer、词表和规则版本变化应使不相容缓存退出可用集合。\\\\n\\\\n## 验证语言与服务两层边界\\\\n\\\\n用小词表枚举合法延伸，覆盖跨 token 的转义、UTF-8、嵌套结构、EOS 和空合法集合；再测试分支回滚、取消和模型切换。格式通过后还应检查 schema/业务层约束，不把语法解析成功当作内容正确。\\\\n\\\\n性能区分首次规则编译、每 token mask 生成、传输与设备计算。将复杂约束预热移出计时，可以回答稳态问题，但不能支持冷启动同样快的结论。长输出、不同 grammar 与输入分布需要独立保留验证。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 分布、行映射与随机流\\\\n\\\\n按行采样需要明确每个输出对应哪一行分布；归档允许用索引将多个输出映射到同一概率行，以避免重复存储。相同分布可以产生多个样本，不能把“复用概率行”误作“复用同一个随机结果”。输入概率与 logits 的处理路径也不同。\\\\n\\\\n语义参考可以先将合法 logits 变成分布，应用截断并归一化，再按随机数在累计质量中选择类别。归档的融合 GPU 路径描述为无需显式排序的拒绝采样；Python 包装文件不足以证明其全部设备内循环，因此下面的逻辑是分布定义，不冒充设备源码。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n为每个输出确定概率行和该请求的截断条件\\\\n按明确顺序建立合法类别集合，去掉被屏蔽质量并归一化\\\\n从该请求的随机流取得随机状态，按目标分布生成类别\\\\n回传到对应请求/位置，并按实际随机数消费推进随机状态\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## 截断顺序是语义\\\\n\\\\n归档区分先 top-k 再 top-p 与联合处理。二者不能仅按名字视为等价。设原分布 [0.5,0.3,0.2]、k=2、p=0.6：先截 top-k 并归一化为 [0.625,0.375]，再取 top-p 时首类已够 0.6；若 top-p 的质量阈值在原分布上定义，则需前两类，再与 top-k 相交仍保留两类。这说明参考算法必须写明阈值使用哪份归一化分布。\\\\n\\\\n显式随机种子与偏移由调用方维护，重复传入同一状态不会自动产生新的随机流。确定性实现标志也不表示每次采样都应产生同一个类别；比较需要固定输入、映射和随机状态。独立请求的流随 batch 重排是否保持身份，是设计与验证条件，见[批量采样](../algorithms/batched-sampling.md)与[结构化输出](../algorithms/structured-output.md)。\\\\n\\\", \\\"excerpt_ranges\\\": [[0, 943]], \\\"range_unit\\\": \\\"zero-based half-open \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# K-ALG-011：批量采样：概率变换、请求随机性与行映射\\\\n\\\\n采样器消费每个请求自己的条件分布；向量化改变执行形态，不能改变参数、随机状态或输出归属。\\\\n\\\\n## 采样之前已经发生了什么\\\\n\\\\nlogits 的行并不总与 batch 请求一一对应。prefill 可能输出所有输入行，但只需取最后有效位置；投机验证需要一段位置；并行候选又可能让一个请求占多行。先确定“请求、逻辑位置、分支 → logits 行”的映射，才能定义每行的采样参数。\\\\n\\\\ntemperature 缩放、重复惩罚、禁用 token、grammar mask、top-k 和 top-p 是有顺序的变换。top-p 根据排序后的归一化概率保留最小累计概率集合；它与 temperature 一般不交换。对所有 logits 同加常数不改变 softmax，乘常数则改变熵。temperature＝0 应按规定的 greedy 语义处理，不是直接除以零。\\\\n\\\\n## 用一个小分布说明顺序\\\\n\\\\n设原分布为 0.5、0.3、0.2。top-p＝0.6 通常保留前两项并重新归一化；若先用低温使第一项概率超过 0.6，则只保留第一项。若 grammar 禁止第一项，必须在合法集合中重新定义概率与截断，否则可能得到空集合或错误归一化。空合法集合应对应协议中的失败或恢复策略，不能静默抽取非法 token。\\\\n\\\\n## 每请求的随机轨迹\\\\n\\\\n共享一个按 batch 行连续消耗的随机流，会使请求输出受其他请求的加入、取消与重排影响。若任务要求调度无关的可复现性，可将随机流绑定请求种子、逻辑位置和采样次数；投机接受、拒绝重采样也要有明确的子序列定义。普通 seed 固定只保证某种执行路径下的随机初始化，并不自动提供这种更强性质。\\\\n\\\\n在设备上批量完成筛选、采样和 EOS 判断可避免逐请求主机同步。不同 top-k、top-p、temperature 可以表现为逐行参数，不必每种参数拆一个 batch。若算法内部成本随参数变化，分组可能提高效率，但分组后的逆映射必须保持请求身份。\\\\n\\\\n## 哪些验证支持哪种结论\\\\n\\\\ngreedy 的目标是匹配规定的 argmax 与平局规则。随机采样的目标是匹配分布，可以对固定小概率向量比较频率、支持集与置信区间。相同 seed 的单条文本不同，不能单独证明分布错误；非法 token、概率质量丢失或请求间随机状态串用，则是不同层面的明确问题。\\\\n\\\\n## 分支与词表分片的额外映射\\\\n\\\\n多样本、beam 和投机树让同一请求有多条逻辑路径。temperature、grammar、随机状态与 logits 行必须按请求、分支、位置共同索引；分支重排后只更新 token 行而遗漏采样参数，会产生数值看似正常但语义错误的结果。被淘汰、完成或 padding 的行不能继续消费正式随机子序列。\\\\n\\\\n词表沿设备分片时，argmax/top-k 和概率归一化需对应全词表。各片独立归一化或采样后再拼接，通常不是同一分布。分布式归约的平局规则、dtype 与完成顺序需要进入采样参考，而不只检查单设备算子。\\\\n\\\\n## 稳定性与有效吞吐\\\\n\\\\n极大 logits、全非法 mask、边界 top-p 和等概率平局是必要的区分输入。对有限精度实现，记录最大值减除、归约与阈值比较的精度；采样核快但改变支持集时不能算作合法优化。\\\\n\\\\n统计验证使用固定小分布和多次独立抽样，再对真实请求检查输出身份与协议。为了得到更好性能而缩短输出、重复相同随机流或忽略失败行，会改变有效工作量；应以满足任务条件的已提交结果计吞吐。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# K-ALG-006：投机解码：分布保持、状态提交与收益模型\\\\n\\\\n投机用便宜候选换取目标模型的并行验证；真正推进系统的是被确认的前缀，而非写入过缓存的全部 token。\\\\n\\\\n## 问题、不变量与设计轴\\\\n\\\\n问题：自回归 decode 每步只产生一个 token，设备在小 batch 下远未饱和；用某种更便宜的过程提出多个候选，让目标模型一次验证，可以把串行步数换成并行宽度。要回答的是\\\\\\\"候选从哪来、验证到哪一步为止算确认、未确认的状态怎样撤销、什么时候不值得\\\\\\\"。\\\\n\\\\n不变量：输出分布与不投机时的目标分布一致（随机采样下通过接受/修正规则，greedy 下通过逐位比较）；只有已确认前缀进入下一轮可见历史；KV、递归状态、语法状态、随机状态和输出缓冲按同一确认边界提交或回滚；候选位置与其 KV 的一步偏移被正确处理。\\\\n\\\\n成本项：草稿生成、目标验证（随候选数增长）、拒绝后的撤销与回收、调度与图桶的变长处理、以及被挤占的其他请求预算。收益是每次目标前向的期望确认 token 数，它随接受分布与 batch 大小变化。\\\\n\\\\n设计轴：草稿来源（独立小模型 / 目标特征预测 / 无模型的 n-gram 或 prompt lookup / 多头并行）；候选结构（单链 / 树）；验证规则（greedy 比较 / 随机接受修正）；深度与宽度的决定方式（固定 / 按近期接受分布在线调整 / 按 batch 占用率关闭）；状态撤销机制（延迟回收页 / 快照恢复 / 重算）。无模型草稿把草稿成本降到查表，前提是输出中存在可从上文复制的片段，接受率随任务变化很大；它在设计轴上是\\\\\\\"零草稿成本、低接受率\\\\\\\"的一端。本章后续展开各点的前提与代价。轴上未列点同样合法。\\\\n\\\\n## 两种语义不能混用\\\\n\\\\ngreedy 场景中，草稿提出若干 token，目标模型对相同前缀并行计算这些位置，保留直到首次不符合目标 greedy 选择的位置。随机采样场景中，简单比较 sampled token 是否相等会改变分布。设草稿条件分布为 q，目标为 p，候选 x 的接受概率是 min(1,p(x)/q(x))；拒绝后从与 max(p−q,0) 成比例的剩余分布抽样。在双方共享正确条件前缀等前提下，这类修正才保持目标分布。\\\\n\\\\ntemperature、惩罚、top-k/top-p、grammar 都改变用于采样的分布。接受比必须对应实际应用这些处理后的 p 和 q，而不能将原始 logits 的概率与截断采样混合。分布等价也不意味着在相同 seed 下逐 token 一致，随机数消耗路径可能不同。\\\\n\\\\n## 缓存推进是一次提交\\\\n\\\\n草稿提出 γ 个候选时，目标验证要读已确认状态并计算候选对应的状态。假设只接受前 a 个，后续候选的 KV 虽然可能已经写入，但不能成为下一轮的可见历史。系统应有“已保留容量、已写入状态、已确认长度”三个概念；拒绝处理改变后两个的有效范围，物理页可延迟回收。\\\\n\\\\n还存在一个常见的一步偏移：预测某个 token 的 logits 来自其前一位置的隐藏状态，而该 token 自己的 KV 需要在它作为输入参与前向后才存在。额外抽样出的 bonus token 未必已经具有 KV。调度器必须按实际计算位置推进，不能直接将输出 token 数当成新增 KV 数。\\\\n\\\\n递归模型的状态被覆盖后不能像 append-only KV 一样只缩短长度。投机需要递归状态快照、可恢复检查点或重新计算。grammar 状态、随机状态、输出缓冲区也必须与接受边界一起提交。\\\\n\\\\n## 收益不是接受率一个数\\\\n\\\\n设一轮草稿成本 Dγ、验证 Vγ、管理 Hγ，最终平均产出 E[L] 个已确认输出，单位 token 成本约 (Dγ＋Vγ＋Hγ)/E[L]。只有它低于普通目标 decode 的成本才有收益。在独立、固定接受率 α 的简化模型中，带 bonus 的 E[L] 可写为 Σᵢ₌₀^γ αⁱ；真实接受事件有条件相关性，应测接受长度分布。\\\\n\\\\n举例：普通每 token 10 个时间单位；γ＝4，一轮草稿 8、验证 13、管理 3、平均产出 3，则新成本 8，理想吞吐提高 25%。若 batch 扩大后普通 decode 已降为 6，同一投机配置反而更慢。额外目标验证 token 还可能占据其他请求的计算预算。\\\\n\\\\n## 和调度、图执行的关系\\\\n\\\\n不同请求接受长度不同，使下一轮 query 数、页增量、输出数量都变长。图可以按最大候选数保留固定缓冲区，但 mask 和 valid lengths 必须表达真实提交范围。调度器可按近期接受分布调整 γ，将额外验证预算给高收益请求；这是一项在线资源分配问题，不能把 γ 固定为越大越好。\\\\n\\\\n## 草稿来源、树形预算与指标\\\\n\\\\n草稿可以来自小模型、特征预测或其他明确的候选生成过程。[EAGLE v1](../sources/S-EAGLE.md) 将目标特征和已采样的下一 token 一起用于后续特征草稿，说明条件输入需要包含影响下一状态的不确定性。草稿结构改变不取消目标验证、拒绝修正与共同提交的要求。\\\\n\\\\n树形验证可以在一次目标前向中覆盖多个候选位置，但每个节点只看到自己的祖先。链式接受率与树的候选通过比例不是同一个指标；多条兄弟候选通常只有一条进入最终路径。更有用的是目标前向数、已确认输出长度、无效验证量、管理开销和端到端 goodput。\\\\n\\\\n动态选择深度/宽度时，除近期接受分布，还要考虑其他请求的预算、KV/递归快照、graph 桶与草稿启动成本。低接受率、目标 batch 已充分利用或草稿占用关键资源时，应允许关闭投机。成本下降必须与目标分布/质量及服务约束共同确认。\\\\n\\\\n故障或重试后，应从已确认路径及相应随机/grammar 状态继续；不能把之前已写入但被拒绝的候选重新当作有效历史。针对每种候选生成与验证协议保留独立小分布参考，不能把论文的理论等价性直接视为本项目实现已经正确。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-SPEC：Fast Inference from Transformers via \\\"knowledge/system-semantics/tokenization-io.md\\\", \\\"sha256\\\": \\\"1dea61a1f632805cb90873e747cb3079230a7b6bab76b17b4281662b82367565\\\", \\\"reading_scope\\\": \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# K-SYS-007：输入输出语义：Tokenizer、Chat Template 与流式文本\\\\n\\\\n模型处理的是规范化后的 token/特征序列，服务协议必须精确保存从用户输入到模型输入再到输出文本的映射。\\\\n\\\\n## 文本序列化就是模型输入的一部分\\\\n\\\\nchat messages 通过模板加入角色边界、回合终止和生成提示。BOS/EOS 是否由模板插入、是否还由 tokenizer 自动插入，会改变最终 token 序列。把 messages 直接拼接成普通字符串不等价于训练时的对话格式；工具调用和多模态 placeholder 也可能有专门语法。\\\\n\\\\ntokenizer 版本、normalization、特殊 token 配置和 truncation 策略共同定义输入。Unicode 看起来相同的字符串可以有不同字节或规范化结果。前缀缓存应基于模型实际消费的规范表示，而不是仅以 UI 字符串或字符长度判断。\\\\n\\\\n## Padding 与长度\\\\n\\\\n不同模型/框架对左 padding、右 padding、位置编码和末 token logits 抽取有不同约定。有效输入、模型位置编码与缓存推进需要分别表示；attention mask 与各位置/缓存字段的形状、padding 规则和更新顺序按所选实现核对。长输入截断是任务语义选择：丢开头可能丢系统指令，丢尾部可能丢用户问题；服务不能把截断当成纯性能优化而不记录。\\\\n\\\\n## 增量 detokenization\\\\n\\\\ntoken 边界不等于字符边界，一个 token 也可能包含多个字符或不完整字节片段。逐 token 独立 decode 再串接未必等于整段 decode。流式解码器需要保留未稳定后缀，直到能输出有效文本片段。\\\\n\\\\nstop string 可能跨多个 token 或多个网络 chunk，检测要保留足够后缀。若协议规定不把 stop string 发给用户，就必须延迟可能构成其前缀的字符，而不能先发出再撤回。EOS、最大 token 数与 stop string 是不同终止原因，对 usage 计数和 finish reason 有不同影响。\\\\n\\\\n## 多模态沿用同一原则\\\\n\\\\n图片/音频预处理版本、采样率、裁剪、patch 网格和文本占位符顺序一起定义模型输入。输出音频也需要样本位置、编码格式和 chunk 顺序。输入输出正确性可以在 CPU 上固定这些中间表示，成为后续内核优化共享的语义参考。\\\\n\\\\n## 制品一致性跨过文本与模型边界\\\\n\\\\n输入档案绑定 tokenizer/processor 的固定版本、模板、特殊 token 表、词表与模型 embedding/output head 的维度。两套 tokenizer 都能产生合法整数 ID，不代表它们对同一文本产生相同模型输入。输出解码还要使用与输入和模型一致的语义，不能在版本切换中混用旧 decoder 与新词表。\\\\n\\\\n工具回合需要保留角色、工具调用身份、参数序列化和结果顺序。应用层把结果格式化为文本的方式可能改变 token 序列，即使业务上看起来表达同一个 JSON 对象。复用判断应从最终模型输入出发；会话 ID 只提供查找入口，不能独立证明 KV 等价。\\\\n\\\\n## 增量输入与 tokenization 的边界\\\\n\\\\n对新增文本片段单独分词再拼接，未必等于对完整文本分词：边界附近可能发生合并或 normalization 差异。只有实际 tokenizer 的增量契约或稳定边界得到证明时才能复用已分词前缀。多轮服务可以缓存经过完整序列化与分词的共同前缀，但模板新增的回合标记也要包含在对应身份中。\\\\n\\\\n截断和输入限额应在明确的计量单位执行。字节、Unicode 字符、token、图像 patch 和音频采样点不能混用；模型最大上下文与服务可承受的资源预算也不一定相同。若拒绝、截断或分段，响应协议和测量记录要保留实际发生的处理。\\\\n\\\\n## 优化 CPU 路径时保持的关系\\\\n\\\\n分词批处理、缓存规范化结果、原生实现和进程池都可能减少输入开销，但必须保持 token IDs、offset/模态对齐和特殊 token 行为。缓存键包含会影响结果的配置；缓存容量和保存敏感输入的边界由服务隔离要求约束。并发分词不能让可变模板或 processor 缓冲在请求间串用。\\\\n\\\\n对照输入包含空消息、非 ASCII、组合字符、特殊 token 样式文本、跨片段合并、多个工具结果及不同 padding。输出验证包含跨 token 的 UTF-8 片段、跨 chunk stop string、取消前最后一段内容与 usage/finish reason。测试比较规范 token/特征和协议事件，避免只比较屏幕上看起来相同的文本。\\\\n\\\\n若 CPU 输入阶段已成为瓶颈，按 [主机运行时](host-runtime.md) 分配有界工作池；若模型计算支配总时延，复杂输入缓存可能仅增加容量和失效逻辑。测量时把输入排队、实际 CPU 服务与模型等待分开，才能判断优化是否改变用户时间。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-CHAT：Transformers：Chat templates](../sources/S-CHAT.md)：Chat template 将消息序列变为包含角色边界、特殊 token \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# K-ALG-024：多样本与搜索分支：父子状态、评分与共同提交\\\\n\\\\n一个请求可以产生多个候选前缀，但 beam search、多样本采样和投机树具有不同目标。它们可以共享不可变前缀的计算与存储，不能因此共享可变输出、随机轨迹或未经确认的后续状态。\\\\n\\\\n## 先定义分支的目标\\\\n\\\\n| 方式 | 分支用于什么 | 不能据此推断 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 多样本采样 | 从规定分布得到多个样本 | 选出其中最高分结果仍服从原单样本分布 |\\\\n| Beam search | 按累计评分保留有限候选 | 它等价于普通随机采样或保证全局最优序列 |\\\\n| 投机树 | 提供候选以减少目标模型串行验证次数 | 验证多个节点后可以任意挑一条并保持目标分布 |\\\\n\\\\nbeam 的评分可包括累计 log 概率、长度处理和约束；平局、EOS 和停止条件都属于搜索定义。改变长度惩罚或保留宽度会改变结果，不能作为纯执行优化隐藏。多样本的重排/筛选目标也应在任务契约中写明。\\\\n\\\\n## 父子映射与状态所有权\\\\n\\\\n每个分支记录稳定身份、父分支/分叉位置、逻辑 token 路径、模型状态版本、累计评分、grammar/RNG 和终止状态。压紧 batch 后的槽位只是临时映射；所有采样参数、logits 行与结果都要反向映射到同一分支。\\\\n\\\\n满页的共同前缀可共享只读 KV，追加需要私有尾页或写时复制。淘汰分支后，引用为零仍不代表设备/传输已结束。设定每 token 状态为 128 KiB，共同前缀 1024 token，4 个分支各追加 16 token；忽略碎片，分别完整复制需要 520 MiB，共享前缀需要 136 MiB。这个节省不消除每条不同路径的后续计算。\\\\n\\\\n两个独立样本应有符合要求的独立随机子序列。仅复制相同 RNG 状态而不定义分叉规则，可能让多个样本重复相同随机轨迹。若要求调度无关可复现，随机身份还要绑定逻辑分支和采样位置，而非当前 batch 行。\\\\n\\\\n## 树形 attention 的可见关系\\\\n\\\\n验证树可以把多个候选位置放到一次前向，但每个 query 只能看到原始前缀及本路径的祖先，不能看到兄弟分支。假设 A/B 都是根前缀的下一 token，C 是 A 的子节点，则 C 可以依赖 A，不能依赖 B。物理行连续不等于它们属于同一序列。\\\\n\\\\n一个节点作为输入被计算后，所得 logits 表示它之后的条件分布；根后的第一个候选由根前缀末行的分布验证。被输出或被接受的 token 自身是否已经具有 KV，要按实际计算位置判断。接受路径、有效状态与已分配容量分别管理，避免树压紧时引入一步偏移。\\\\n\\\\n## 草稿来源和验证规则分开\\\\n\\\\n[EAGLE v1](../sources/S-EAGLE.md) §3–4 研究在目标模型特征上生成草稿，并引入提前一步的已采样 token 来消除下一特征的不确定性；它也采用树形候选组织。这说明草稿可以来自不同表示，目标分布是否保持仍取决于验证与重采样协议。\\\\n\\\\n对链式随机投机，接受与拒绝修正使用相同条件前缀下实际的 p、q；对多候选树，还要明确候选如何生成、选择顺序以及拒绝后分布怎样更新。不能把链式 p/q 规则直接套在任意 top-k 树，再任意选择获批分支。grammar、temperature 和截断变换也必须与这些分布对应。\\\\n\\\\n## 提交与回滚跨过多个状态族\\\\n\\\\n保留一条路径时，KV/递归状态、grammar、随机状态、评分和输出缓冲共同转移到相同边界。非保留节点的物理空间等待最后使用者结束后回收。SSM 等覆盖式状态不能仅通过缩短 token 长度回滚，需要快照、检查点或重算。\\\\n\\\\n如果多个分支结果被拼接为新提示，新的上下文通常需要重新处理或按明确的复用算法构建；把两条独立路径的 KV 直接拼接不是一般有效的 join。流式输出也只应发布不会被后续搜索替换的内容；无法证明稳定时，应延迟提交或按协议处理结果修订。\\\\n\\\\n## 资源预算与验证\\\\n\\\\n宽度增加会扩展 logits、mask、候选状态、验证 token 和排序开销。深度增加可能改善一次接受长度，也可能耗费更多无效草稿；应按已确认输出衡量成本。分支与其他请求共享预算时，还要观察公平性和整体 goodput。\\\\n\\\\n在小词表上穷举短序列作为 beam/采样参考，再对同一叶路径比较树形与独立前向。覆盖兄弟泄漏、平局、EOS、重排、部分取消和分支淘汰后复用；随机协议检验支持集与频率。最后在独立任务上检查质量与时延，不能用候选数量或共享比例代替收益。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- \\\"knowledge/system-semantics/serving-recovery.md\\\", \\\"sha256\\\": \\\"f551fa1f1e6213469c856a880839eefff504fb39f4dd692000b2df80a20a7f5e\\\", \\\"reading_scope\\\": \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# K-SYS-014：推理服务恢复：提交边界、执行组与重试身份\\\\n\\\\n恢复首先要确定哪些工作已经成为外部可依赖的结果、哪些状态仍可信，以及谁有权继续提交。检测到超时或重新启动进程，都不能独立回答这些问题。\\\\n\\\\n## 三个边界分别记录\\\\n\\\\n计算边界表示哪些输入位置已经生成完整模型状态；确认边界表示投机/搜索后哪些 token 属于保留路径；外部提交边界表示服务已经按协议发布的内容。它们可能不同。prefill 末行可以产生一个 token，但该 token 自身的 KV 未必已经计算；网络发送返回也不等于客户端已消费。\\\\n\\\\n恢复描述至少包含请求与尝试身份、模型/adapter/输入配置、已确认 token、可重建的共同状态位置，以及需要继续的随机、grammar 和输出状态。只保存 KV 字节无法恢复任意请求；只保存 token 也不自动恢复任意递归模型、分支状态或已经发生的外部动作。\\\\n\\\\n可重算的模型状态与不可重复的业务结果分开处理。固定前缀可以帮助重建 KV，但跨 backend 重算是否逐位一致取决于数值契约。若协议需要断线续传，应有明确的游标、去重与确认规则；否则应报告失败或重新请求，不能默认已经获得“恰好一次”交付。\\\\n\\\\n## 故障矩阵决定恢复路线\\\\n\\\\n| 故障位置 | 首先确认 | 合法的恢复或终止方式 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 输入处理进程失败 | 是否已准入、输入是否可重放 | 从固定输入重做未提交部分，清理预留 |\\\\n| 单个计算 rank 退出 | 执行组是否还拥有一致状态 | 停止受影响组，从共同提交点重建或明确失败 |\\\\n| KV 传输部分完成 | 目标范围和源副本的有效性 | 撤销未提交目标，重传或从可恢复前缀重算 |\\\\n| 源在接管期间失效 | 目标是否完成且已获提交权 | 按协议完成接管；否则使用其他副本或重建 |\\\\n| 磁盘/压缩读取失败 | 哪些对象可重建、哪些记录必须保留 | 失效对应缓存；不能把未完成解码当作可用状态 |\\\\n| 客户端断线 | 哪些内容已发出、协议能否确认消费 | 依协议取消、续传或失败，不猜测客户端进度 |\\\\n\\\\n每条路线同时说明输出处理和资源清理。最后一个错误通常只是连锁超时，诊断要保留最早失败、rank 状态、操作序号和已经完成的范围。\\\\n\\\\n## 执行组恢复与单请求恢复不同\\\\n\\\\nTP/EP 等组内的 ranks 必须执行相容的操作序列。一个 rank 的失败不能让其他 ranks 继续把局部结果当作完整层；请求取消也不能让某个 rank 单独跳过 collective。根据固定通信库的错误处理契约终止或重建受影响资源，并让调度器停止向失效组提交新工作。\\\\n\\\\n重建可以重新加载模型、重建 communicator/执行上下文，再恢复合法状态。已经失效的设备句柄、注册区、页表和图对象不能仅因地址看起来相同就继续使用。较大的执行组能处理更大模型，但故障影响范围与恢复时间也随组织方式改变。\\\\n\\\\n## 迁移期间只允许一份提交权\\\\n\\\\n[Llumnix v1](../sources/S-LLUMNIX.md) §4.2 描述了分阶段复制、目标预留和迁移异常处理；它利用 append-only KV 隐藏部分复制时间。窗口覆盖、递归状态和可回滚分支不自动满足这个前提，需冻结或另行保存恢复版本。\\\\n\\\\n应用需要明确源端何时停止提交、目标何时获得提交权，以及确认丢失时如何判断。新尝试带独立代次，旧节点的迟到消息不能重新获得当前请求的提交权。多个控制节点也必须提供一致的授权规则，不能各自根据本地超时决定同时接管。\\\\n\\\\n最后源副本释放与目标提交之间的窗口必须有恢复依据。可以保留源直到确认、依赖已经完整的其他副本，或允许从持久输入重算；选择取决于故障模型与成本。内存内迁移本身不能保证机器同时失效后仍有持久恢复能力。\\\\n\\\\n## 重试预算和过载反馈\\\\n\\\\n重试可能与原任务同时消耗资源，且常发生在系统已过载时。控制并发尝试、总时间预算和退避，避免把一次网络或节点故障变成请求放大。幂等传输 ID 处理重复范围，逻辑请求 ID 处理重复提交；它们是不同层次。\\\\n\\\\n恢复后需重新检查 deadline、质量和容量。如果剩余时间已无法满足任务，不应无条件重试直到某次成功再隐藏此前失败。故障恢复实验与正常稳态性能分开报告，也要度量恢复期间对其他请求造成的影响。\\\\n\\\\n## 验证可观察的不变量\\\\n\\\\n在预留后、部分传输后、目标发布前后、输出提交前后分别注入失败。检查请求终态唯一、输出序号连续、旧代次不覆盖新状态、未完成缓冲不被复用，以及资源最终回到声明的稳态基线。对随机生成，明确要求相同轨迹还是相同分布；对可重算缓存，检查恢复位置和其他状态族的交集。\\\\n\\\\n低失败率、短请求可能适合失败后重做；长请求、严格交互连续性或昂贵状态可能需要更多检查点、副本与接管协议。多种方案都要把恢复成本计入 SLO 与容量，而不是只比较无故障时的速度。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-LLUMNIX：Llumnix](../sources/S-LLUMNIX.md)：§4 通过分阶段 append-only KV \\\"c2f88bc9746ac25586fc6700aaf0f5a8d043a1b1f4aee99dfdee02e1ef468aab\\\", \\\"reading_scope\\\": \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# K-TOOLS-006：正确性 Oracle：函数参考、状态变形与服务契约\\\\n\\\\n正确性验证需要一组互补的 oracle：数值函数、状态转换、采样分布和外部协议分别有可检查的关系。\\\\n\\\\n## 函数参考与实现独立性\\\\n\\\\n简单稠密 attention、高精度矩阵路径或原模型 forward 可以作为数值参考，前提是输入、mask、位置和权重一致。参考若调用与被测实现相同的页表索引或共享同一个错误 processor，就失去对应维度的独立性。独立性应具体说明到逻辑组件，而不是仅说“另一个测试”。\\\\n\\\\n## 变形关系覆盖状态\\\\n\\\\n同一请求独立执行与放入不同顺序的 batch 应保持规定语义；整段 prefill 与分块 prefill 应一致；冷缓存与合法前缀命中后继续应一致；页的物理重新排列不应改变逻辑结果。这些关系改变执行组织而保持函数，适合在 CPU 小实例上穷举边界。\\\\n\\\\n取消后，新请求使用回收槽应与全新槽执行一致；两个不同 adapter 的相同 prompt 应分别对应各自参考；window rollover 前后应对应同一绝对位置定义。每种关系都来自具体状态模型，可以发现“常见样例都对”时仍隐藏的错误。\\\\n\\\\n## 概率与协议需要其他 Oracle\\\\n\\\\n随机采样用固定小分布检验支持集、归一化和频率，投机检验目标分布关系；单条文本 exact match 不足以证明概率正确。服务协议检查 chunk 顺序、终止事件、stop string、usage、错误和背压，不能只看返回了 HTTP 200。\\\\n\\\\n质量指标还包括 ASR 词错误率、视觉任务准确性、图像质量或语音一致性。数值近似通过小张量容差与任务质量合格各提供不同支持。一个完整工程验收把这些 oracle 组合起来，而不是让一个最终布尔值遮住具体覆盖。\\\\n\\\\n## 组合覆盖来自相交的状态边界\\\\n\\\\n各机制单独正确，不能推出组合正确。先列出它们共同触及的对象：分页与前缀共享共同管理尾块；投机与 grammar 共同管理未提交分支；异步执行与取消共同管理在途缓冲；量化与迁移共同管理尺度与布局。测试应覆盖交界上的状态转换，而不是机械地对全部参数做笛卡尔积。\\\\n\\\\n例如“前缀共享＋异步取消”的判别场景：A/B 共享完整前缀，各自追加不同 token；取消 A 后立即把它可回收的私有槽分给 C；延迟 A 的完成通知；继续 B/C。参考分别从各自逻辑 token 全量重建，检查 B 未被污染、C 不接收 A 的迟到输出、共享页未提前回收。这个时序可以区分身份错误、引用错误和完成事件错误。\\\\n\\\\n## 性质测试与并发调度\\\\n\\\\n把物理页排列、batch 排序、分块边界和无关请求插入作为变形维度，保持模型函数与有效输入不变。生成器需要包含跨页、非整除尾部、零长度边界和最大合法范围，并在失败时保留最小可复现输入。变形关系本身也要有前提：改变采样种子不要求文本一致，改变模型版本不再保证缓存等价。\\\\n\\\\n并发测试要控制完成顺序，包括旧工作晚于新工作返回、多个 stream 的不同事件次序、传输部分完成、取消与提交竞争。随机压力有发现价值，确定性的受控时序更便于解释；两者都不能以一次未出现错误证明所有竞态已消除。\\\\n\\\\n## 长时间运行检查守恒关系\\\\n\\\\n资源池满足总量=空闲+活跃占用+在途保护+保留但可解释的占用，各项不能重复计数。测试经过多轮分配、共享、驱逐、取消和失败恢复后，未完成工作清空时应回到预先声明的稳态基线。缓存刻意保留导致的驻留与不可达对象泄漏不同；观察 RSS 不下降时，需要先区分 allocator 保留和真实失去所有者。\\\\n\\\\n同时检查请求终态唯一性、输出序号连续性、最多一次的外部提交，以及失败是否留下可复用却未初始化的块。故障注入应落在定义过的协议边界；若业务允许重试，参考需要包含重试身份与结果提交规则，不能用最终“有输出”掩盖重复响应。\\\\n\\\\n## 独立保留验证检查什么\\\\n\\\\n开发样例用于定位和调参，最终保留样例覆盖未参与选择的形状、长度、输入分层和状态时序。对低位路径，先用固定量化参数的独立公式排除实现错误，再检查原模型质量；对概率路径，先用小分布验证采样关系，再做统计检验。独立性说明到具体组件：参考可以共用权重文件，但不能在要验证页表索引时共用被测页表逻辑。\\\\n\\\\n知识章节提出的是 oracle 和区分实验。只有实际任务执行这些检查，才能记录相应通过或失败；章节写得完整、结构检查通过，都不能被标记成目标引擎的正确性证据。\\\\n\\\\n## 从任务要求派生检查，而不改变要求\\\\n\\\\n先区分用户契约、组件数学定义和本次测试实现。用户要求完整历史或精确输出时，测试驱动不能为了可运行而截短历史、忽略出错请求或改成更宽松的质量定义。测试参考和观测器可以修订，但修订说明应回答原检查错在何处、新检查如何恢复原契约、哪些旧结论受到影响。\\\\n\\\\n构建初期没有现成生产引擎可以作为唯一 oracle 时，按可独立核对的边界建立组合参考：固定权重与前处理下的函数参考；小状态空间中的索引/所有权关系；端到端协议与任务质量。组件参考只覆盖其声明的域，不会因局部结果正确而自动补齐整个服务的验证。接口问题分别见 [服务协议](../system-semantics/service-protocol.md)、[请求身份](../system-semantics/request-batch-identity.md) 与 [取消和完成](../system-semantics/cancellation-resource-completion.md)；张量语义见 [基础算子](../algorithms/operator-primitives.md) 和 [后端选择](../frameworks/attention-backends.md)。\\\\n\\\\n## 验证器也要能拒绝已知错误\\\\n\\\\n这里的负对照是主动构造一个违反既定要求的输出或轨迹，检查验证器是否确实拒绝；它检验的是测试辨别力，不是目标引擎性能。数值比较可改变一个应该被检查的元素；协议比较可漏掉终止事件、重复提交或调换两个请求的输出；状态检查可把迟到完成放到槽位复用之后。干预应改变所研究的错误维度，保留其他条件，避免一次同时破坏全部格式而无法知道哪个检查生效。\\\\n\\\\n一个可手工复算的身份反例是：预期集合包含不同请求 A、B，合法输出分别为 17、99。实际轨迹却返回 A=17、B=17。若驱动只保留 A 或将二者错误合并成一个槽，已保留样本的比较可以全部通过，但完整任务不正确。要求 expected、observed 与 terminal 的身份集合在任务定义下对应，同时检查重复、缺失、额外结果和每个身份的内容，才能排除这个假通过。该例是本轮设定的逻辑反例，不代表新运行观测。\\\\n\\\\n空结果集也不能被“全部元素正确”的逻辑真值接受为完成。检查至少要区分应有结果是否齐全、每个结果是否有效、每个状态/终止是否唯一。若协议允许中途取消或部分输出，则其合法预期由取消契约定义，不能随实现返回什么而变化。\\\\n\\\\n## 保留请求、会话和运行的失败范围\\\\n\\\\n一个多轮会话中的后续输入可能依赖前序输出。前一轮失败后，后续未执行属于缺失或被阻断，不能计作验证成功，也不能从预先约定的会话集合中删除。分别报告计划的逻辑轮次、实际发起请求、接纳、拒绝、完成、取消、超时与质量失败；请求指标的分母使用实际发起还是计划请求，必须由任务预先声明，会话成功则需满足该会话的全部必要依赖。请求级条件成功率不能代替整段会话成功率。\\\\n\\\\n检查工具若只记录局部抽样，需声明抽样对象和未覆盖范围。固定 seed 帮助复现特定轨迹，不会自动覆盖所有并发时序；一次完成所有正向样例，也不证明验证器能识别遗漏字段或丢失请求。正向参考与针对性负对照分别提供正确样例和已知错误的辨别证据；选择哪些检查取决于任务与所选机制，不要求每个探索实验复跑全部协议和状态场景。\\\\n\\\\n## 检查缺陷对旧证据的影响\\\\n\\\\n发现检查器遗漏身份、错误比较数值或计时边界错误后，先定位受影响的规则、测试版本和实验，不把所有历史结果笼统清零，也不继续沿用被该缺陷支持的结论。如果原始输出、事件与输入完整，修订后的检查可以重分析这些数据，并保留新旧检查身份；缺少所需信息时必须重跑相应路径。\\\\n\\\\n这是一条证据使用原则，不声称当前运行时会自动发现所有传播关系。设计者应显式说明哪些数值结论、机制判断或系统选择需要复核。检查器修复完成仅恢复了判断能力，不能代替候选通过修订后的检查。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- The downstream\\\\napplications can then organically consume the structured\\\\noutputs to perform followup interactions with the system.\\\\nConstrained decoding (Deutsch et al., 2019; Kuchnik et al.,\\\\n2023) is a commonly adopted method for structured gen-\\\\neration. It guarantees the output of LLMs adheres to the\\\\nspecified structure through only allowing tokens that con-\\\\nform to the structure to be generated at each decoding step.\\\\nAt each step, constrained decoding first scans the entire\\\\nvocabulary to identify invalid tokens and sets their probabil-\\\\n1Carnegie Mellon University 2NVIDIA 3Shanghai Jiao Tong\\\\nUniversity 4University of California, Berkeley. In LLMs, tokens serve as the basic input and\\\\noutput units. Each token represents a fixed string but may\\\\nnot correspond to a complete semantic unit or may break a\\\\nUnicode character (Wang et al., 2019), creating challenges\\\\nfor structured text generation. At each step, the model\\\\nproduces a logits vector across its vocabulary, which is then\\\\nconverted into a probability distribution using the softmax\\\\nfunction (Bridle, 1989). A sampler then selects the next\\\\ntoken from this distribution.\\\\nConstrained decoding guides the structure of LLM-\\\\ngenerated text by restricting available tokens at each step,\\\\nas illustrated in Figure 2. At each step, tokens that would\\\\nviolate the required structure are identified as invalid. Their\\\\nlogits are set to −∞, effectively assigning them zero prob-\\\\nability after the softmax operation and preserving the rel-\\\\native probabilities of other valid tokens. This ensures that\\\\nonly valid tokens are sampled. Efficiently identifying and\\\\nmasking invalid tokens is essential, as it directly impacts\\\\ngeneration speed.\\\\n2.2\\\\nContext-free Grammar and Pushdown Automata\\\\nContext-free grammar (CFG) (Chomsky, 1956) is widely\\\\nused to define structures in structured generation. This\\\\nbyte-level design allows each character edge to include one\\\\nor more bytes, handling irregular token boundaries and sup-\\\\nporting tokens containing sub-UTF8 characters. The au-\\\\ntomaton’s structure is optimized to accelerate matching,\\\\nas described in §3.4. In the preprocessing phase, we gen-\\\\nerate an adaptive token mask cache, as detailed in §3.1,\\\\nwhich accelerates runtime mask generation by precomput-\\\\ning context-independent tokens. The effectiveness of this\\\\ncache is further enhanced by context extension in §3.2. At\\\\nruntime, the token mask cache quickly generates most of the\\\\nmask, while the persistent execution stack in §3.3 efficiently\\\\nprocesses the rest context-dependent tokens. Additionally,\\\\nmask generation and LLM inference are overlapped in §3.5\\\\nto minimize the overhead of constrained decoding. Once the\\\\nLLM generates a new token under the mask constraint, this\\\\ntoken is then used to update the stack state of the pushdown\\\\nautomaton for the next mask generation.\\\\n3.1\\\\nAdaptive Token Mask Cache\\\\nTo accelerate the generation of the token mask cache, the\\\\nadaptive token cache categorizes tokens into two types\\\\n(Figure 4): context-independent tokens, which constitute\\\\nthe vast majority and can be pre-computed, and context-\\\\ndependent tokens, which require slower, on-the-fly process-\\\\ning but are relatively few. This token classification relates to\\\\nhow tokens are validated by the pushdown automaton. We\\\\nfound that, considering the transition of the stack state, the\\\\nprocess of matching tokens to the automaton can be divided\\\\ninto three categories:\\\\n1. The matching process expands into a child rule, push-\\\\ning new elements onto the stack.\\\\n2. The matching process advances within the current rule,\\\\nupdating the stack top node to a new position.\\\\n3. The matching process reaches the end of the current\\\\nrule and returns to a parent rule, popping elements\\\\nfrom the stack.\\\\nValidating tokens in the former two cases only relies on the\\\\nstack top node, which represents the position within the cur-\\\\nrent rule, so we define these tokens as context-independent\\\\ntokens. The tokens in the third type, however, requires\\\\ninspecting the entire running stack in validation, and are\\\\ndefined as context-dependent tokens. For every node of the\\\\npushdown automaton, there is a set of context-independent\\\\ntokens with this node being at the top of the stack at run-\\\\ntime, and their validity can be determined ahead of time.\\\\nTherefore, we precompute the validity of these tokens and\\\\nstore them in a cache with the stack top node as the key,\\\\nwhich we refer to as the adaptive token mask cache. It also\\\\nadaptively selects the most efficient storage format based on\\\\nthe cache’s contents, as explained in the next paragraph.\\\\nAt runtime, we retrieve the validity of context-independent\\\\ntokens directly based on the top of the stack to generate the\\\\ntoken mask. The remaining few context-dependent tokens\\\\nare validated by executing the pushdown automaton with\\\\nthe full stack. If parallel stacks exist due to the ambiguity\\\\nof the grammar, the token masks for every stack is merged\\\\ninto a final token mask by finding the union of the accepted\\\\ntokens in each mask. The computation for the token mask\\\\nis significantly reduced because our method do not need\\\\nto check context-independent tokens at runtime. Experi-\\\\nments show that context-dependent tokens account for only\\\\na minor proportion, amounting to less than 1% (1134 out of\\\\n128k) for the Llama-3.1 model using JSON grammar.\\\\nAdaptive storage.\\\\nThe token mask cache adopts an adap-\\\\ntive storage format to reduce memory usage, as illustrated\\\\nin Figure 5. For each automaton node, the token mask cache\\\\ndivides the vocabulary into three parts: the accepted context-\\\\nindependent tokens, the rejected context-independent to-\\\\nkens, and the context-dependent tokens. Since these three\\\\nparts together cover all tokens, it is sufficient to store only\\\\nthe two smaller subsets. We observe that, for a set of context-\\\\nindependent tokens, they tend to be either almost entirely\\\\naccepted, namely accept-heavy cases, or almost entirely\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 5 ---\\\\nXGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine For Large Language Models\\\\nAccept-heavy Cases: Store \\\\nReject-heavy Cases: Store \\\\nEqual Cases: Very rare, store bitsets\\\\nFigure 5. The adaptive storage format. In accept-heavy cases, we\\\\nstore the rejected tokens and context-dependent tokens. In reject-\\\\nheavy cases, we store the accepted tokens and context-dependent\\\\ntokens. In rare cases where two kinds of tokens are equal, we\\\\ncompress the accepted and rejected tokens into a bitset of the\\\\nvocabulary size.\\\\nrejected, namely reject-heavy cases. This arises because, if\\\\nwildcards can be matched from the current node, such as the\\\\nwildcard [ˆ\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\]* in the rule of string, nearly all tokens are\\\\nvalid; whereas if the node only accepts a few specific charac-\\\\nters, nearly all tokens are invalid. Based on this observation,\\\\nwe designed the following adaptive storage format:\\\\n1. For accept-heavy cases, we store the rejected context-\\\\nindependent tokens and context-dependent tokens in\\\\ntwo arrays.\\\\n2. For reject-heavy cases, we store the accepted context-\\\\nindependent tokens and context-dependent tokens in\\\\ntwo arrays.\\\\n3. For rare cases where the accepted and rejected tokens\\\\nare roughly equal, we store the accepted and rejected\\\\ncontext-independent tokens and compress them into a\\\\nbitset matching the vocabulary size.\\\\nThus, in both accept-heavy and reject-heavy cases, the adap-\\\\ntive storage format only requires storing a small subset of\\\\ntokens, significantly reducing memory usage. In practice,\\\\nwe will enumerate the three storage types, calculate their re-\\\\nspective costs, and choose the storage type with the smallest\\\\nsize. For Llama-3.1 model and JSON grammar, this adap-\\\\ntive storage method can effectively reduce the total memory\\\\nusage to 0.2% (from 160 MB to 0.46 MB).\\\\nAdditionally, when multiple parallel stacks exists, we need\\\\nto merge the token masks. The merging algorithm of token\\\\nmasks is optimized based on storage type, as shown in Algo-\\\\nrithm 1. For an accept-heavy mask (many accepted tokens,\\\\nstoring only rejected tokens), it intersects the rejected tokens\\\\nwith PartialRej. For a reject-heavy mask (many rejected\\\\ntokens, storing only accepted tokens), it combines accepted\\\\ntokens with PartialAcc. In the final mask, the rejected to-\\\\nkens are the set difference PartialRej \\\\\\\\ PartialAcc. This\\\\nalgorithm limits set operations to small token subsets, thus\\\\nenhancing efficiency.\\\\nAlgorithm 1 Efficiently Merge Token Masks\\\\nInput:\\\\nToken masks for k parallel stacks {Mi\\\\n=\\\\n(Acci, Reji)}k\\\\ni=1, vocabulary V.\\\\nOutput: The final token mask M = (Acc, Rej).\\\\nInitialize PartialAcc ←∅, PartialRej ←V\\\\nfor i = 1 to k do\\\\nif Mi is accept-heavy then\\\\nMi only stores rejected token list Reji\\\\nPartialRej ←PartialRej ∩Reji\\\\nelse\\\\nMi only stores accepted token list Acci\\\\nPartialAcc ←PartialAcc ∪Acci\\\\nend if\\\\nend for\\\\nM ←(V \\\\\\\\ (PartialRej \\\\\\\\ PartialAcc),\\\\nPartialRej \\\\\\\\ PartialAcc)\\\\n3.2\\\\nContext Expansion\\\\nAlthough the adaptive token mask cache effectively re-\\\\nduces the number of tokens checked at runtime, checking\\\\nall context-dependent tokens remains an efficiency bottle-\\\\nneck at runtime. To further reduce the number of context-\\\\ndependent tokens, XGrammar introduces context expansion,\\\\nwhich leverages the grammar’s context information to reject\\\\nmore context-dependent tokens during preprocessing, as\\\\nshown in Figure 6.\\\\nAs described in the last section, a token is context-dependent\\\\nwhen we reach the end of the current rule during matching,\\\\nbut there is still a remaining part of the token that requires\\\\nfurther checking by returning to the parent rules. However,\\\\nthrough analysis of the grammar, we can observe that in a\\\\nlarge portion of the cases, the remaining part of a token is\\\\ninvalid. This is because, for many rules, when they reach\\\\ntheir end, there are only a limited number of positions they\\\\ncan return to within their parent rules, and the set of strings\\\\nthat can be further matched from those positions is also\\\\nlimited.\\\\nBased on this observation, context expansion precomputes,\\\\nfor each rule, the set of strings that can be accepted after\\\\nreturning to the parent rules, called the expanded suffix.\\\\nThe remaining unmatched part of the context-dependent\\\\ntokens should either be a prefix of the expanded suffix or\\\\nstart with the expanded suffix. Otherwise, they are rejected.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 6 ---\\\\nXGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine For Large Language Models\\\\n[8] '\\\\\\\"'\\\\n[9] [^\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\]\\\\n[10] '\\\\\\\"'\\\\nm\\\\nh\\\\nstr:\\\\nl\\\\nExpanded Suffix\\\\nfor str\\\\nBefore Context Expansion\\\\n,\\\\nAfter Context Expansion\\\\nContext-dependent\\\\n\\\\\\\"ab\\\\na\\\\\\\"b\\\\n\\\\\\\",\\\\n\\\\\\\"]\\\\nContext-dependent\\\\n\\\\\\\",\\\\n\\\\\\\"]\\\\nContext-independent\\\\n(Rejected)\\\\n\\\\\\\"ab\\\\na\\\\\\\"b\\\\nRejected by the\\\\nexpanded suffix\\\\n]\\\\nFigure 6. The context expansion. Each rule obtains a set of ex-\\\\npanded suffices, representing the set of strings that must be\\\\nmatched after completing this rule. The remaining unmatched\\\\npart of the context-dependent tokens should either be a prefix of\\\\nthe expanded suffix or start with the expanded suffix. Otherwise,\\\\nthey are rejected.\\\\nThis filtering process effectively reduces the number of\\\\ncontext-dependent tokens by eliminating those that would\\\\nfail in higher-level rule contexts. Applied to the Llama-3.1\\\\nmodel and JSON grammar, this technique reduces context-\\\\ndependent tokens by 90% (from 1,134 to 120).\\\\nAlgorithm 2 describes the context expansion process that\\\\nfinds the expanded suffix of each rule. For a rule R, we\\\\nutilize a finite state automaton (FSA) Actx\\\\nR (ctx is the abbre-\\\\nviation for context) to represent the expanded suffix, and that\\\\nis extracted from the pushdown automata. We first find all\\\\nedges e = (s, t) in the pushdown automata that references\\\\nR and belongs to rule R′. R′ is not necessarily different\\\\nfrom R. However, we will not\\\\nconsider edges in the subgraph that reference other rules\\\\nto avoid recursive references between rules, so the edges\\\\nin the extracted subgraph will only have character labels.\\\\nAlgorithm 2 Extract the Expanded Suffix Automaton\\\\nInput: Pushdown automaton P, rule R\\\\nOutput: Expanded context FSA Actx\\\\nR for R\\\\nInitialize Actx\\\\nR as an empty FSA\\\\nfor edge s\\\\nR\\\\n−→t in P referencing R do\\\\n{ Aδ is an FSA for the partial result }\\\\nInitialize Aδ as an empty FSA, visited ←{}\\\\nAdd node t to Aδ\\\\nEXTRACTONE(t, Aδ, visited)\\\\n{ Merge the partial result into the final result }\\\\nActx\\\\nR ←FSAUNION(Actx\\\\nR , Aδ)\\\\nend for\\\\nfunction EXTRACTONE(start, Aδ, visited)\\\\nif start in visited then\\\\nreturn\\\\nend if\\\\nAdd start to visited\\\\n{ Stop search for nodes with rule-referencing edges }\\\\nif start is a final node in P or\\\\nhas an edge referencing another rule then\\\\nMark start as final in Aδ\\\\nreturn\\\\nend if\\\\n{Now all outward edges of start are character edges}\\\\nfor edge start\\\\nc−→end from start do\\\\nAdd end and start\\\\nc−→end to Aδ\\\\nEXTRACTONE(end, Aδ, visited)\\\\nend for\\\\nend function\\\\nIf a node has both character edges and edges referencing\\\\nother rules, we will stop the search at this node. The ex-\\\\ntracted subgraph is then merged into Actx\\\\nR . This process is\\\\nrepeated for all rules, and the extracted Actx\\\\nR is used to reject\\\\ncontext-dependent tokens cannot match any string in it after\\\\nfinishing matching rule R.\\\\nAlthough we do not consider rule-referencing edges when\\\\nextracting the expanded context automata, this algorithm\\\\ncan still extract many useful context information. That is\\\\nbecause the inlining optimization introduced in §3.4 inlines\\\\nfragment rules into their parent rules, reducing the need to\\\\ncheck into child rules to reject context-dependent tokens.\\\\n3.3\\\\nPersistent Execution Stack\\\\nAs the grammar engine still needs to handle context-\\\\ndependent tokens, we need to efficiently execute the push-\\\\ndown automata for these tokens. Additionally, we also need\\\\nto execute the pushdown automata for preprocessing the\\\\ncontext-independent token sets for all positions in the push-\\\\ndown automata. In both cases, we need to maintain multiple\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 7 ---\\\\nXGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine For Large Language Models\\\\n[0] array\\\\n[3] str\\\\nNode l\\\\n[5] str\\\\nNode l\\\\nNode d\\\\n[0]<array>\\\\n[3]<str>\\\\nNode l\\\\n[0]<array>\\\\n[5]<str>\\\\nNode l\\\\nStacks of \\\\nthe current step\\\\nStacks from\\\\nprevious steps\\\\n[0]<array>\\\\nNode d\\\\nNode a\\\\nRoot\\\\nNode a\\\\nPersistent\\\\nExecution\\\\nStack\\\\nFigure 7. The persistent stack organizes multiple matching stacks\\\\nfrom the current step, as well as stacks from previous steps, into a\\\\nsingle tree. It reduces memory consumption and supports rolling\\\\nthe state back to previous steps.\\\\nparallel stacks and branch out as we match the characters\\\\nin each token. To support efficient state branching, we in-\\\\ntroduce the persistent execution stack (Driscoll et al., 1989)\\\\nto manage the multiple stacks and efficiently execute the\\\\npushdown automata. It can also manage the stacks from\\\\nprevious time points and enable the state rollback opera-\\\\ntion, effectively speeding up the execution of the pushdown\\\\nautomata on a set of tokens.\\\\nAs shown in Figure 7, the persistent execution stack man-\\\\nages a set of stacks, which are either the parallel stacks\\\\nfrom the current time point or the stacks from previous time\\\\npoints, into a single tree, and every stack is represented by a\\\\npath from the root node on the tree. The stack top node is\\\\nstored as a pointer to the node in the tree. Since the stacks\\\\nfrom adjacent time points often share most of the deeper\\\\nelements and only a few nodes are pushed or popped, this\\\\nmerging avoids memory redundancy for storing multiple\\\\nstacks. When matching a new character from a token, we\\\\nmay need to split the stack into multiple stacks due to the\\\\nambiguity of the grammar, each corresponding to a different\\\\nexpansion of grammar rules. In this case, we only need to\\\\nsplit the branch for that stack instead of copying the whole\\\\nstack, which reduces the overhead of state branching.\\\\nAdditionally, the persistent execution stack enables fast state\\\\nrollback by maintaining the stack from previous time points.\\\\nAt runtime, a sliding window of history is maintained. To\\\\nroll back to a previous state, we only need to change the\\\\ncurrent stack pointers, which requires constant time. This\\\\nrollback operation is particularly useful for checking a large\\\\nset of tokens, as many tokens share a common prefix with\\\\nother tokens, such as read, ready, and reader all sharing\\\\nthe prefix read. All the checked tokens are sorted in lexico-\\\\ngraphical order to find the maximum length of the common\\\\nprefixes. Then the tokens are checked one by one, and be-\\\\nfore checking each token, the state rolls back to just after\\\\nthe common prefix with the previous token. Therefore, we\\\\ncan avoid the redundant checks of these common prefixes,\\\\nreducing the number of characters that need to be checked.\\\\nFor Llama-3.1 model and JSON grammar, this approach\\\\nreduces the number of characters that need to be checked\\\\nacross the entire vocabulary to 30%, significantly speeding\\\\nup the preprocessing stage.\\\\nThe rollback operation enables more applications with\\\\nefficient structured generation.\\\\nThere are many LLM ap-\\\\nplications that involve rolling back the output to a previous\\\\ntoken. For instance, the jump-forward decoding (Yin et al.,\\\\n2024) requires retokenization, which involves rolling back\\\\nsome tokens in the context and then inserting new tokens. To\\\\nensure structured generation can continue after rolling back\\\\ntokens, we can roll back the automaton state simultaneously\\\\nwith the output token rollback. There are also many LLM\\\\napplications that requires LLMs generate in a tree struc-\\\\nture, such as in Tree-of-thought (Yao et al., 2024), SGLang\\\\n(Zheng et al., 2024), and the speculative model in the spec-\\\\nulative decoding algorithm SpecInfer (Miao et al., 2024).\\\\nWe can maintain the automata state for every branch of the\\\\noutput tree, and when the output branches, we can quickly\\\\nsplit the automaton state, maintaining separate matching\\\\nstates for each output branch. This branching is fast because\\\\nwe only need to maintain the stack top pointer on the tree\\\\nfor every branch. Therefore, the persistent execution stack\\\\nenables us to ensure efficient structured generation for all\\\\nthese applications.\\\\n3.4\\\\nPushdown Automata Structure Optimizations\\\\nWe will perform additional optimizations to improve the\\\\nstructure of pushdown automata to speed up the efficiency\\\\nof final execution. These optimizations draw from tradi-\\\\ntional compiler optimization concepts, but we find them\\\\nparticularly useful for efficient constrained decoding.\\\\nRule inlining.\\\\nThere could be many fragment rules, i.e.\\\\nrules with only a few elements, in the specified context-free\\\\ngrammar, which are then converted into small FSA in the\\\\npushdown automaton. On the one hand, this increases the\\\\nambiguity of the grammar since we need to inspect into\\\\nthese fragment rules and check during the execution of the\\\\npushdown automata. On the other hands, during context\\\\nexpansion, references to fragment rules are not considered,\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 8 ---\\\\nXGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine For Large Language Models\\\\nso the extracted context automata will be smaller. We will\\\\nmiss the opportunity to reject context-dependent tokens\\\\nbased on the structure of these fragment rules.\\\\nTo address this issue, we introduce an automatic inlining\\\\nstrategy (Scheifler, 1977) for fragment rules. We iteratively\\\\npick rules that do not reference other rules and inline them\\\\ninto the parent rules. To avoid the explosion of the automa-\\\\nton size, we limit the size of the inlined rule and the size\\\\nof inlined result to constants. This inlining process almost\\\\neliminated fragment rules, thereby improving the efficiency\\\\nof token checking and enhancing the effectiveness of the\\\\ncontext expansion.\\\\nPushdown automata node merging.\\\\nFor pushdown au-\\\\ntomata, in many cases, the ambiguity comes from multiple\\\\noutward edges of a node with the same label. When match-\\\\ning tokens, if we arrive at this node, and the next character\\\\njust matches the label, the matching stack will be split into\\\\nmultiple stacks, one for each outward edge. The increase in\\\\nthe number of stacks increases the computation as we need\\\\nto check the context-dependent tokens for each stack and\\\\nmerge the token masks. To reduce this kind of ambiguity,\\\\nthe node merging algorithm merges the subsequent nodes\\\\nthat satisfy: a) they are pointed to by edges with the same\\\\nlabel originating from the same point b) they are not pointed\\\\nto by other edges.\\\\nAdditionally, the epsilon edge also increases the ambigu-\\\\nity of the matching process. An epsilon edge s\\\\nϵ−→t in\\\\nthe automata means that the matching process can directly\\\\nmove from s to t without consuming any characters. If the\\\\nmatching process arrives at s, the execution stack will split\\\\ninto two stacks, one with s at the top and the other with t,\\\\nboth of which can continue matching. To reduce this kind\\\\nof ambiguity, the node merging algorithm also merges the\\\\nnodes s and t into a single node, as long as s has no other\\\\noutward edge or t has no zero inward edge.\\\\nThese two optimizations preserves the equivalence of the\\\\nautomaton, but reduces the number of nodes and edges. At\\\\nruntime, the number of stacks and the computation required\\\\nfor token checking are reduced, speeding up the mask gen-\\\\neration process.\\\\n3.5\\\\nOverlapping Mask Generation and LLM\\\\nInference\\\\nWith the optimizations mentioned above, the token mask\\\\ngeneration process is significantly accelerated, but it still\\\\nrequires CPU computation. To further eliminate the over-\\\\nhead of constrained decoding, we overlap the computation\\\\nfor mask generation with the LLM inference process, as\\\\nshown in Figure 8. We observed that the mask generation\\\\nprocess and LLM inference process can be overlapped. That\\\\nis because the mask generation only requires CPU, and only\\\\nLLM Prefilling\\\\nBuild Mask Cache\\\\nCPU\\\\nGPU\\\\nMask\\\\nGen\\\\nSampling\\\\nLLM Decoding\\\\nMask\\\\nGen\\\\nSampling\\\\nSync\\\\nSync\\\\nFigure 8. Overlapping building the mask cache with LLM prefill-\\\\ning, and mask generation with LLM decoding to minimize the\\\\noverhead.\\\\ndepends on the previously generated tokens. The LLM infer-\\\\nence process except the sampling stage only requires GPU,\\\\nand also only depends on the previously generated tokens.\\\\nTherefore, we can parallelize the mask generation process\\\\non the CPU with the LLM inference process on the GPU.\\\\nWe will synchronize before sampling, and the GPU will ob-\\\\ntain the mask from the CPU and perform masked sampling\\\\nto generate the new token. Additionally, the preprocessing\\\\nstage can also be overlapped with the LLM prefilling stage,\\\\nwhere the LLM processes the prompt. This orchestration\\\\nbetween CPU and GPU ensures that the token restrictions\\\\nare applied seamlessly, with almost zero overhead for LLM\\\\ninference. In practice, the time for mask generation is less\\\\nthan the time for LLM inference, so the mask generation\\\\nprocess will not become the bottleneck of the generation\\\\nprocess.\\\\n4\\\\nEVALUATION\\\\nWe implement XGrammar in 12,000 lines of core C++ code,\\\\nand we provide Python bindings to facilitate seamless inte-\\\\ngration with LLM inference frameworks. On average, the input has\\\\n139 tokens, and the generated output has 53 tokens.\\\\nThe experiment results are shown in Figure 10. XGrammar\\\\nachieves the best TPOT among all baselines for both JSON\\\\nSchema and CFG. The computation of vLLM and llama.cpp\\\\nis hindered by their grammar engines’ longer preprocessing\\\\nand per-token processing time. The decrease in TPOT speed\\\\nin vLLM becomes particularly noticeable with larger batch\\\\nsizes. This is because a larger batch size leads to higher\\\\nthroughput, putting greater pressure on grammar processing\\\\non the CPU side. Overall the XGrammar-based structured\\\\ngeneration solutions can bring up to 80x output token rate\\\\ncompared to existing solutions. This proves the effective-\\\\nness of XGrammar’s system optimizations and its co-design\\\\nwith the serving engine.\\\\nWe also study the effectiveness of XGrammar across differ-\\\\nent models in end-to-end serving scenarios. As the result\\\\nshown in Table 1, for various models, SGLang integrated\\\\nwith XGrammar consistently outperforms its integration\\\\nwith Outlines, demonstrating the robustness of XGrammar’s\\\\neffectiveness across model architectures. This experiment\\\\nalso provides direct evidence that XGrammar outperforms\\\\nother constrained decoding library when running on the\\\\nsame serving engine.\\\\nAdditionally, we examine the overhead of XGrammar’s con-\\\\nstrained decoding in end-to-end scenarios by measuring\\\\nperformance on the MLC-LLM engine with and without\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 10 ---\\\\nXGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine For Large Language Models\\\\n1\\\\n16\\\\n32\\\\nBatch Size\\\\n101\\\\n102\\\\n103\\\\n104\\\\nTime per output token (ms)\\\\n187\\\\n790\\\\n1432\\\\n11\\\\n93\\\\n164\\\\n7\\\\n10\\\\n12\\\\n6\\\\n9\\\\n12\\\\nJSON Schema\\\\n1\\\\n16\\\\n32\\\\nBatch Size\\\\n101\\\\n102\\\\n103\\\\n104\\\\nTime per output token (ms)\\\\n185\\\\n736\\\\n1252\\\\n137\\\\n2311\\\\n×\\\\n7\\\\n10\\\\n13\\\\n6\\\\n9\\\\n12\\\\nContext-free Grammar (JSON)\\\\nllama.cpp\\\\nvLLM (w/ Outlines)\\\\nSGLang (w/ XGrammar)\\\\nXGrammar Engine\\\\nFigure 10. We begin\\\\nby implementing a baseline using a pushdown automaton\\\\nparser without any optimizations, where each token mask is\\\\ngenerated by checking the entire vocabulary to determine\\\\nwhether parsing can proceed. Building on this baseline, we\\\\nprogressively add the optimizations described in this paper,\\\\nnamely node merging, the adaptive token mask cache, rule\\\\nTable 4. Impact of XGrammar on structured generation tasks.\\\\nXGrammar ensures 100% syntactic correctness of the generated\\\\noutputs.\\\\nTask\\\\nAccuracy w/o\\\\nAccuracy w/\\\\nXGrammar\\\\nXGrammar\\\\nFunction calling\\\\n62%\\\\n100%\\\\nXML code generation\\\\n80%\\\\n100%\\\\ninlining, and context expansion. For each configuration, we\\\\nmeasure the average mask generation time on the CFG (un-\\\\nconstrained JSON) task with the Llama-3.1 8B model and\\\\nthe json-mode-eval dataset. As shown in Table 3, the results\\\\nshow that the adaptive token mask cache has the greatest\\\\nimpact in terms of speedup, while other techniques, includ-\\\\ning node merging, rule inlining, and context expansion, also\\\\nyield noticeable improvements.\\\\n4.4\\\\nImpact of XGrammar on Structured Generation\\\\nTasks\\\\nXGrammar can improve the generation quality of LLMs by\\\\nensuring that the output strictly adheres to the given format.\\\\nWe evaluate the impact of XGrammar on two strcutured\\\\ngeneration tasks: function calling (i.e., JSON generation\\\\nguided by a JSON schema) and XML code generation. For\\\\nfunction calling, we use the json-mode-eval dataset, while\\\\nfor XML code generation, we rely on a synthetic dataset.\\\\nWe measure the syntactic correctness of the generated func-\\\\ntion calling outputs and XML code using LLaMA-3.1 8B.\\\\nAs shown in Table 4, XGrammar significantly improves\\\\ngeneration accuracy. We observe that without XGrammar,\\\\nthe model often includes additional explanations alongside\\\\nthe intended code output, or the generated JSON contains\\\\nan unexpected type. This makes the output unsuitable for\\\\ndirect use by downstream applications. XGrammar avoids\\\\nthis issue by enforcing grammar constraints.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n--- PAGE 11 ---\\\\nXGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine For Large Language Models\\\\n5\\\\nRELATED WORK\\\\nSeveral works looked at algorithm improvements for struc-\\\\ntured generation. (Koo et al., 2024) proposes an algorithm\\\\nto convert character-level pushdown automata to token-level\\\\npushdown automata. (Wang et al., 2023) specifies LLM\\\\noutput structure through prompting. (Rozi`ere et al., 2024;\\\\nChaudhary, 2023; Li et al., 2023) explore finetuning LLMs\\\\nfor higher quality structured generation. XGrammar’s ap-\\\\nproach is orthogonal to these methods and can be combined\\\\nwith these approaches.\\\\nThere has also been some previous work focusing on con-\\\\nstrained decoding. Some methods use regex to represent\\\\nsyntax, such as lm-format-enforcer (Gat, 2024), but they\\\\ncannot handle more complex CFGs. Synchromesh (Poesia\\\\net al., 2022) and llama.cpp (Gerganov, 2023) utilizes LR\\\\nparser and PDA respectively to handle CFG and generate\\\\nthe mask, but requires checking the entire vocabulary at\\\\nruntime, which incurs large overhead. Outlines (Willard\\\\n& Louf, 2023) handles the grammar through a lexer and\\\\nparser, and uses caching to accelerate mask generation, but\\\\nit only considers the most recent lexer token, which may\\\\nlead to incorrect judgments when LLM tokens span across\\\\nmultiple lexer tokens (Appendix A in (Koo et al., 2024)).\\\\nSyncode (Ugare et al., 2024) uses a lexer and parser with a\\\\ncache spanning multiple lexer tokens, but requires all tokens\\\\nto be processed offline, leading to substantial preprocessing\\\\noverhead. In this work, XGrammar leverages a PDA to sup-\\\\nport CFGs and introduces an adaptive token mask cache to\\\\nadaptively handle tokens during preprocessing and runtime,\\\\ncombining other system optimizations to achieve minimal\\\\noverhead in both stages.\\\\nGuidance (Guidance-ai, 2024), LMQL (Beurer-Kellner,\\\\n2023), SGLang (Zheng et al., 2024) provide flexible ways\\\\nto declare the structures. XGrammar is complementary to\\\\nthese improvements and can be used as the backend engine\\\\nto speedup their execution.\\\\nLLM serving engines (MLC team, 2023a; Zheng et al.,\\\\n2024; Kwon et al., 2023a; hiworldwzj et al., 2024) em-\\\\nploy various techniques to support efficient LLM generation\\\\nfor multiple concurrent users, including engine-level tech-\\\\nniques such as continuous batching (Yu et al., 2022) for\\\\ndyanmic request scheduling, and low-level KV cache tech-\\\\nnique PagedKVCache (Kwon et al., 2023a) for efficient\\\\nmemory management. Also, AICI (Moskal et al., 2024)\\\\nproposes a CPU-GPU parallel computation paradigm to ac-\\\\ncelerate structured generation. These LLM serving engines\\\\ncan leverage XGrammar for efficient, structured generation\\\\non top of their existing LLM inference techniques.\\\\n6\\\\nCONCLUSION\\\\nWe proposed XGrammar, a flexible and efficient structured\\\\ngeneration engine for LLMs. XGrammar separates the\\\\nvocabulary into context-independent tokens and context-\\\\ndependent ones. It prechecks the context-dependent tokens\\\\nand stores the result in an adaptive token mask cache. We\\\\nfurther introduce a persistent stack to speed up the execu-\\\\ntion of context-dependent checks. Finally, we co-design\\\\nthe grammar engine with LLM inference to overlap gram-\\\\nmar execution with GPU computation. Our system greatly\\\\nspeeds up the token mask generation process in token mask\\\\nand enables zero overhead structure generation in end-to-\\\\nend LLM inference flows. We hope our system can enable\\\\na broader range of structure generation across platforms.\\\\nACKNOWLEDGEMENTS\\\\nThis work was supported in part by NSF award CNS-\\\\n2211882, and gifts from OctoAI, Qualcomm, and CMU\\\\nopensource software fellowships. See the License for the\\\\nspecific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.\\\\n\\\\n⚠️ Note that this file is in Markdown but contain specific syntax for our doc-builder (similar to MDX) that may not be\\\\nrendered properly in your Markdown viewer.\\\\n\\\\n-->\\\\n\\\\n# Chat templates\\\\n\\\\nThe [chat basics](./conversations) guide covers how to store chat histories and generate text from chat models using [`TextGenerationPipeline`].\\\\n\\\\nThis guide is intended for more advanced users, and covers the underlying classes and methods, as well as the key concepts for understanding what's actually going on when you chat with a model.\\\\n\\\\nThe critical insight needed to understand chat models is this: All causal LMs, whether chat-trained or not, continue a sequence of tokens. When causal LMs are trained, the training usually begins with \\\\\\\"pre-training\\\\\\\" on a huge corpus of text, which creates a \\\\\\\"base\\\\\\\" model.\\\\nThese base models are then often \\\\\\\"fine-tuned\\\\\\\" for chat, which means training them on data that is formatted as a sequence of messages. The chat is still just a sequence of tokens, though! The list of `role` and `content` dictionaries that you pass\\\\nto a chat model get converted to a token sequence, often with control tokens like `<|user|>` or `<|assistant|>` or `<|end_of_message|>`, which allow the model to see the chat structure.\\\\nThere are many possible chat formats, and different models may use different formats or control tokens, even if they were fine-tuned from the same base model!\\\\n\\\\nDon't panic, though - you don't need to memorize every possible chat format in order to use chat models. Chat models come with **chat templates**, which indicate how they expect chats to be formatted.\\\\nYou can access these with the [`apply_chat_template`] method. Let's see two examples. Both of these models are fine-tuned from the same `Mistral-7B` base model:\\\\n\\\\n<hfoptions id=\\\\\\\"template\\\\\\\">\\\\n<hfoption id=\\\\\\\"Mistral\\\\\\\">\\\\n\\\\n```py\\\\nfrom transformers import AutoTokenizer\\\\n\\\\ntokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(\\\\\\\"mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1\\\\\\\")\\\\nchat = [\\\\n  {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"Hello, how are you?\\\\\\\"},\\\\n  {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"assistant\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"I'm doing great. How can I help you today?\\\\\\\"},\\\\n  {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"I'd like to show off how chat templating works!\\\\\\\"},\\\\n]\\\\n\\\\ntokenizer.apply_chat_template(chat, tokenize=False)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n```md\\\\n<s>[INST] Hello, how are you? [/INST]I'm doing great. How can I help you today?</s> [INST] I'd like to show off how chat templating works! [/INST]\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n</hfoption>\\\\n<hfoption id=\\\\\\\"Zephyr\\\\\\\">\\\\n\\\\n```py\\\\nfrom transformers import AutoTokenizer\\\\n\\\\ntokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(\\\\\\\"HuggingFaceH4/zephyr-7b-beta\\\\\\\")\\\\nchat = [\\\\n  {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"Hello, how are you?\\\\\\\"},\\\\n  {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"assistant\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"I'm doing great. How can I help you today?\\\\\\\"},\\\\n  {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"I'd like to show off how chat templating works!\\\\\\\"},\\\\n]\\\\n\\\\ntokenizer.apply_chat_template(chat, tokenize=False)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n```md\\\\n<|user|>\\\\\\\\nHello, how are you?</s>\\\\\\\\n<|assistant|>\\\\\\\\nI'm doing great. How can I help you today?</s>\\\\\\\\n<|user|>\\\\\\\\nI'd like to show off how chat templating works!</s>\\\\\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n</hfoption>\\\\n</hfoptions>\\\\n\\\\nMistral-7B-Instruct uses `[INST]` and `[/INST]` tokens to indicate the start and end of user messages, while Zephyr-7B uses `<|user|>` and `<|assistant|>` tokens to indicate speaker roles. This is why chat templates are important - with the wrong control tokens, these models would have drastically worse performance.\\\\n\\\\n## Using `apply_chat_template`\\\\n\\\\nThe input to `apply_chat_template` should be structured as a list of dictionaries with `role` and `content` keys. The `role` key specifies the speaker, and the `content` key contains the message. The common roles are:\\\\n\\\\n- `user` for messages from the user\\\\n- `assistant` for messages from the model\\\\n- `system` for directives on how the model should act (usually placed at the beginning of the chat)\\\\n\\\\n[`apply_chat_template`] takes this list and returns a formatted sequence. Set `tokenize=True` if you want to tokenize the sequence.\\\\n\\\\n```py\\\\nimport torch\\\\nfrom transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer\\\\n\\\\ntokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(\\\\\\\"HuggingFaceH4/zephyr-7b-beta\\\\\\\")\\\\nmodel = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(\\\\\\\"HuggingFaceH4/zephyr-7b-beta\\\\\\\", device_map=\\\\\\\"auto\\\\\\\", dtype=torch.bfloat16)\\\\n\\\\nmessages = [\\\\n    {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"system\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"You are a friendly chatbot who always responds in the style of a pirate\\\\\\\",},\\\\n    {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"How many helicopters can a human eat in one sitting?\\\\\\\"},\\\\n ]\\\\ntokenized_chat = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors=\\\\\\\"pt\\\\\\\")\\\\nprint(tokenizer.decode(tokenized_chat[0]))\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n```md\\\\n<|system|>\\\\nYou are a friendly chatbot who always responds in the style of a pirate</s>\\\\n<|user|>\\\\nHow many helicopters can a human eat in one sitting?</s>\\\\n<|assistant|>\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nPass the tokenized chat to [`~GenerationMixin.generate`] to generate a response.\\\\n\\\\n```py\\\\noutputs = model.generate(tokenized_chat, max_new_tokens=128) \\\\nprint(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0]))\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n```md\\\\n<|system|>\\\\nYou are a friendly chatbot who always responds in the style of a pirate</s>\\\\n<|user|>\\\\nHow many helicopters can a human eat in one sitting?</s>\\\\n<|assistant|>\\\\nMatey, I'm afraid I must inform ye that humans cannot eat helicopters. Helicopters are not food, they are flying machines. Food is meant to be eaten, like a hearty plate o' grog, a savory bowl o' stew, or a delicious loaf o' bread. But helicopters, they be for transportin' and movin' around, not for eatin'. So, I'd say none, me hearties. None at all.\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n> [!WARNING]\\\\n> Some tokenizers add special `<bos>` and `<eos>` tokens. Chat templates should already include all the necessary special tokens, and adding additional special tokens is often incorrect or duplicated, hurting model performance. When you format text with `apply_chat_template(tokenize=False)`, make sure you set `add_special_tokens=False` if you tokenize later to avoid duplicating these tokens.\\\\n> This isn't an issue if you use `apply_chat_template(tokenize=True)`, which means it's usually the safer option!\\\\n\\\\n### add_generation_prompt\\\\n\\\\nYou may have noticed the [add_generation_prompt](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/internal/tokenization_utils#transformers.PreTrainedTokenizerBase.apply_chat_template.add_generation_prompt) argument in the above examples.\\\\nThis argument adds tokens to the end of the chat that indicate the start of an `assistant` response. Remember: Beneath all the chat abstractions, chat models are still just language models that continue a sequence of tokens!\\\\nIf you include tokens that tell it that it's now in an `assistant` response, it will correctly write a response, but if you don't include these tokens, the model may get confused and do something strange, like **continuing** the user's message instead of replying to it!\\\\n\\\\nLet's see an example to understand what `add_generation_prompt` is actually doing. First, let's format a chat without `add_generation_prompt`:\\\\n\\\\n```py\\\\ntokenized_chat = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False)\\\\ntokenized_chat\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n```md\\\\n<|im_start|>user\\\\nHi there!<|im_end|>\\\\n<|im_start|>assistant\\\\nNice to meet you!<|im_end|>\\\\n<|im_start|>user\\\\nCan I ask a question?<|im_end|>\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nNow, let's format the same chat with `add_generation_prompt=True`:\\\\n\\\\n```py\\\\ntokenized_chat = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)\\\\ntokenized_chat\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n```md\\\\n<|im_start|>user\\\\nHi there!<|im_end|>\\\\n<|im_start|>assistant\\\\nNice to meet you!<|im_end|>\\\\n<|im_start|>user\\\\nCan I ask a question?<|im_end|>\\\\n<|im_start|>assistant\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nWhen `add_generation_prompt=True`, `<|im_start|>assistant` is added at the end to indicate the start of an `assistant` message. This lets the model know an `assistant` response is next.\\\\n\\\\nNot all models require generation prompts, and some models, like [Llama](./model_doc/llama), don't have any special tokens before the `assistant` response. In these cases, [add_generation_prompt](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/internal/tokenization_utils#transformers.PreTrainedTokenizerBase.apply_chat_template.add_generation_prompt) has no effect.\\\\n\\\\n### continue_final_message\\\\n\\\\nThe [continue_final_message](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/internal/tokenization_utils#transformers.PreTrainedTokenizerBase.apply_chat_template.continue_final_message) parameter controls whether the final message in the chat should be continued or not instead of starting a new one. It removes end of sequence tokens so that the model continues generation from the final message.\\\\n\\\\nThis is useful for “prefilling” a model response. In the example below, the model generates text that continues the JSON string rather than starting a new message. It can be very useful for improving the accuracy of instruction following when you know how to start its replies.\\\\n\\\\n```py\\\\nchat = [\\\\n    {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"Can you format the answer in JSON?\\\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"assistant\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": '{\\\\\\\"name\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"'},\\\\n]\\\\n\\\\nformatted_chat = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(chat, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, continue_final_message=True)\\\\nmodel.generate(**formatted_chat)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n> [!WARNING]\\\\n> You shouldn't use [add_generation_prompt](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/internal/tokenization_utils#transformers.PreTrainedTokenizerBase.apply_chat_template.add_generation_prompt) and [continue_final_message](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/internal/tokenization_utils#transformers.PreTrainedTokenizerBase.apply_chat_template.continue_final_message) together. The former adds tokens that start a new message, while the latter removes end of sequence tokens. Using them together returns an error.\\\\n\\\\n[`TextGenerationPipeline`] sets [add_generation_prompt](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/internal/tokenization_utils#transformers.PreTrainedTokenizerBase.apply_chat_template.add_generation_prompt) to `True` by default to start a new message. However, if the final message in the chat has the `assistant` role, it assumes the message is a prefill and switches to `continue_final_message=True`. This is because most models don't support multiple consecutive assistant messages. To override this behavior, explicitly pass the [continue_final_message](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/internal/tokenization_utils#transformers.PreTrainedTokenizerBase.apply_chat_template.continue_final_message) argument to the pipeline.\\\\n\\\\n## Model training\\\\n\\\\nTraining a model with a chat template is a good way to ensure the template matches the tokens the model was trained on. Apply the chat template as a preprocessing step to your dataset. Set `add_generation_prompt=False` because the additional tokens to prompt an assistant response aren't helpful during training.\\\\n\\\\nAn example of preprocessing a dataset with a chat template is shown below.\\\\n\\\\n```py\\\\nfrom transformers import AutoTokenizer\\\\nfrom datasets import Dataset\\\\n\\\\ntokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(\\\\\\\"HuggingFaceH4/zephyr-7b-beta\\\\\\\")\\\\n\\\\nchat1 = [\\\\n    {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"Which is bigger, the moon or the sun?\\\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"assistant\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The sun.\\\\\\\"}\\\\n]\\\\nchat2 = [\\\\n    {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"user\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"Which is bigger, a virus or a bacterium?\\\\\\\"},\\\\n    {\\\\\\\"role\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"assistant\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"A bacterium.\\\\\\\"}\\\\n]\\\\n\\\\ndataset = Dataset.from_dict({\\\\\\\"chat\\\\\\\": [chat1, chat2]})\\\\ndataset = dataset.map(lambda x: {\\\\\\\"formatted_chat\\\\\\\": tokenizer.apply_chat_template(x[\\\\\\\"chat\\\\\\\"], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False)})\\\\nprint(dataset['formatted_chat'][0])\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n```md\\\\n<|user|>\\\\nWhich is bigger, the moon or the sun?</s>\\\\n<|assistant|>\\\\nThe sun.</s>\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nAfter this step, you can continue following the [training recipe](./tasks/language_modeling) for causal language models
